item.title: Democrats' victories in Texas laid bare voter unease over data centers — and signal new hurdles for the industry
item.author: Ben Werschkul
item.description:
Democrats' victories in Texas laid bare voter unease over data centers — and signal new hurdles for the industry
2026-11-06
Por Ben Werschkul
https://finance.yahoo.com/economy/article/democrats-victories-in-texas-laid-bare-voter-unease-over-data-centers--and-signal-new-hurdles-for-the-industry-142918051.html
Democrats' victories in Texas laid bare voter unease over data centers — and signal new hurdles for the industry
A strong showing by Democrats in Texas swept Gina Hinojosa into office as the state's first Democratic governor since 1990 in a contest closely watched by Big Tech companies.
Texas is considered a bellwether for government restrictions on AI data centers and was just one place where deep voter unease over the build-out was on display. Voters across the country passed a series of local ballot measures aimed at restricting construction in the years ahead.
Hinojosa, Texas's first Latina governor, has pledged to impose a moratorium on data center construction in Texas, which accounts for more than 25% of planned US capacity by 2030.
"I want to say something to the powerful people who have gotten very comfortable running this state," she told supporters in her victory speech. "The voters have delivered a mandate for change, and it is change they will get."
Her victory was one of a series of wins for Democrats in Texas. The party is also on track to take control of the Texas House, which would give Hinojosa more power to follow through on restrictions even as the state Senate appears set to remain under Republican control.
"We view the Texas gubernatorial race as particularly important for the next leg of the AI trade," wrote Raymond James's Ed Mills in a pre-election note saying that a strong Democratic showing there "could signal a broader electoral wave while increasing concerns about data center moratoriums and more restrictive AI regulation in the nation's largest planned data center development."
Bank of America called the race "one of the highest impact elections for the entire utility sector."
A race that 'could make a real difference'
Hinojosa made opposition to data center construction a central part of her campaign, charging in one ad that Gov. Greg Abbott "works for" Elon Musk.
She staked out plans for a moratorium on new data center construction, stricter regulations on water and power usage, and an end to tax breaks.
Abbott was seeking his fourth term as governor and said last year he wanted Texas to be the "epicenter of AI development."
More recently, he announced a moratorium of his own and said he would support more stringent requirements on power and water usage. Hinojosa immediately charged that Abbott's new proposals amounted to an "election year pause."
Tobin Marcus of Wolfe Research said Texas "is the one state with enough scale and enough difference between the candidates that it could make a real difference."

item.title: Oil’s war premium is leaking out fast — and the midterms just sped it up
item.author: Jared Blikre
item.description:
Oil’s war premium is leaking out fast — and the midterms just sped it up
2026-11-06
Por Jared Blikre
https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/article/oil-prices-fall-below-90-as-traders-bet-on-iran-war-ending-after-democrats-sweep-midterms-192105228.html
Wall Street's post-midterm party has two no-shows: AI and chip stocks, and oil. Crude is having the far worse time, on track for its worst week since April 2020.
West Texas Intermediate crude (CL=F) settled at $88.12 a barrel on Wednesday, down more than 8% on the day and $16 below Friday's close of $104. Its three-day drop of about 15% is its steepest since November 2021.
Brent (BZ=F), the global benchmark, is near a two-month low. The sell-off came as traders bet on an end to the Iran war after Democrats swept Tuesday's elections.
"The election results may pressure the president to seek to end the war more quickly," the Wells Fargo Investment Institute wrote Wednesday.
Read more: How oil price shocks ripple through your wallet, from gas to groceries
The damage is spreading beyond crude. Gasoline futures (RB=F) are on track for their lowest close since March 10, which is good news for anyone driving to Thanksgiving dinner. The Energy Select Sector SPDR Fund (XLE) is down more than 5%. Refiners Marathon Petroleum (MPC) and Valero (VLO) are down about 8% to 10%.
Even after the slide, oil hasn't given back the whole war. WTI started 2026 near $57 and peaked near $113 on April 7, and it's still roughly 50% above where the year began.
The election angle adds some history. Oil hasn't followed a single script after Trump's elections. Crude rose about 10% from Election Day through the end of November after his 2016 win and about 20% after his 2020 loss, and it fell about 6% after his 2024 win.
The closest echo is 2018, Trump's first midterm, when Democrats took the House. Crude fell about 18% from Election Day through the end of that November, by Yahoo Finance calculations.
Supply hasn't caught up with the peace trade. US diesel stockpiles are at their lowest since 2003, and Wells Fargo noted that gasoline and diesel supplies "remain constrained by the war."
That leaves crude priced for a deal that hasn't happened. Nationwide's chief market strategist, Mark Hackett, says oil is retreating "on hopes for a deescalation in the Iran conflict, even as the diplomatic signals remain ambiguous."

item.title: Big Tech Stocks Soar as Traders Bet Democrats Will Slow AI Spend
item.author: Jeran Wittenstein; Ryan Vlastelica
item.description:
Big Tech Stocks Soar as Traders Bet Democrats Will Slow AI Spend
2026-11-06
Por Jeran Wittenstein; Ryan Vlastelica
https://finance.yahoo.com/technology/ai/articles/big-tech-stocks-soar-traders-170754816.html
(Bloomberg) -- The shares of US technology giants led the market higher on Wednesday as investors bet that a Democrat-controlled Congress will slow the massive spending on artificial intelligence that's eating up free cash flow.
Most Read from Bloomberg
Amazon.com Inc. was up as much as 8.3%, Microsoft Corp. gained 7%, Alphabet Inc. jumped 5.9% and Meta Platforms Inc. advanced 3.6%. Together with Apple Inc., which has avoided heavy AI spending and leaped more than 6%, the five tech behemoths are on pace to add nearly $1 trillion in market value on Wednesday.
Democrats secured majorities in both the House and Senate in Tuesday's election, flipping seats in Republican bastions including South Carolina, Texas and Kansas, and winning down-ballot votes as well to secure control of numerous statehouses and governors' mansions. The party's candidates ran heavily on slowing down AI development, in particular checking the mass construction of data centers required to run the burgeoning technology.
"The market is acting like this represents the end of the AI buildout," said Robert Pavlik, senior portfolio manager at Dakota Wealth Management. "If that means the hyperscalers aren't spending ridiculous amounts of money to build out compute, that means they could become cash-flow positive again."
Exit polls showed that voters strongly oppose new data centers in their communities, Keith Parker, UBS's head of global macro equity strategy and US equity strategy research, wrote in a note to clients on Wednesday. "The blue wave will have implications for equities, with the biggest impact likely coming from an increase in data center regulation at the state level near-term," he wrote.
Shares of Amazon, Microsoft, Alphabet and Meta have been under pressure recently as investors grow increasingly concerned that the hundreds of billions of dollars they're spending on computing infrastructure won't generate sufficient returns. Meanwhile, Amazon, Alphabet and Meta have all seen their free cash flows turn negative, meaning they're spending more on capital expenditures than they're generating from their operations. As a result, the firms are being forced to use the debt and equity markets to fund their spending.

item.title: Why the stock market is unexpectedly rallying in the wake of the Democratic blue wave
item.author: Brian Sozzi
item.description:
Why the stock market is unexpectedly rallying in the wake of the Democratic blue wave
2026-11-06
Por Brian Sozzi
https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/article/why-the-stock-market-is-unexpectedly-rallying-in-the-wake-of-the-democratic-blue-wave-152956959.html
Call it a contrarian move. It has been a riveting 12 hours or so in the markets as investors slice and dice the midterm election outcomes.
Initially, stocks got hammered as the results trickled in. The thinking was that Democrats are less pro-business than Republicans, and since they will control the House and the Senate, there goes the corporate profit miracle that has driven the markets over the past two years.
But something very interesting has emerged after that initial knee-jerk reaction. Stocks are rallying on Wednesday — big-time!
Here are three reasons I think we're seeing this play out.
The AI readthrough
First, the midterm election results threaten to significantly disrupt AI data center expansion as voter backlash over soaring utility bills, grid instability, and water usage drive a sharp political pivot toward tighter regulatory oversight. That is being viewed as a positive for hyperscalers such as Alphabet (GOOG, GOOGL) and Amazon (AMZN) in that they will be forced to pull back on spending, which would boost free cash flow.
Free cash flow declines have been at the heart of the latest AI stock sell-off, so if cash flow outlooks brighten up at the biggest companies driving the market, all the better.
Bye-bye uncertainty
Second, with the elections over, the cloud of uncertainty that had begun to seep into markets in recent weeks has been lifted. Now investors can better place their chips where they see fit.
As the team at the Stocktrader's Almanac pointed out, six months after the past 19 midterm elections, the S&P 500 (^GSPC) has been higher 100% of the time, with an average gain of 14.18%.
Eyes on corporate profits
Third, there is this callout by Goldman Sachs strategist Jan Hatzius today that also gets to the heart of this day-after rally.
Hatzius wrote: "The larger-than-expected majorities could give them slightly greater leverage in negotiations with the White House, but will also dilute the influence of small factions within the Democratic caucus. We expect Democrats to use fiscal deadlines to seek to limit the war with Iran, roll back selected tariffs, and reverse spending cuts enacted last year."
I read that as a pro-corporate bottom line.

Hatzius wrote: "The larger-than-expected majorities could give them slightly greater leverage in negotiations with the White House, but will also dilute the influence of small factions within the Democratic caucus. We expect Democrats to use fiscal deadlines to seek to limit the war with Iran, roll back selected tariffs, and reverse spending cuts enacted last year."
I read that as a pro-corporate bottom line.

item.title: US Treasury Borrows Record $839 Billion in Single Week
item.author: Elizabeth Stanton
item.description:
US Treasury Borrows Record $839 Billion in Single Week
2026-11-06
Por Elizabeth Stanton
https://finance.yahoo.com/economy/policy/articles/us-treasury-borrows-record-839-201757901.html
(Bloomberg) -- The US government borrowed a record $839 billion in a single week via its sales of Treasury bills and notes — both to repay holders of maturing debt and to raise the additional capital needed to finance the federal deficit.
Most Read from Bloomberg
Auctions of bills, floating-rate notes and Treasuries due in two, five and seven years conducted from Oct. 26-30 eclipsed the previous weekly record of $795 billion, set in the same period a year ago, according to Tony Farren, managing director in rates sales and trading at Mischler Financial Group.
The $839 billion is the sum of the 11 auction sizes, and the majority of it went to repay holders of maturing bills. Only $68 billion represented new borrowing by the US government, and it's not close to record levels. Those were set in March and April 2020, when auction sizes surged to finance pandemic response measures, and weekly net new cash peaked at levels around $350 billion.
Gross weekly debt totals vary widely depending mainly on how much debt is slated to mature. This week's record total underscores how the accumulated debt — and the rising cost of financing it — is driving the US government toward ever-larger auction sizes.
"Nothing good is coming from Treasury gross weekly issuance at a record high," Farren said. "The No. 1 risk is that people are going to demand higher yields."
Over the past two years, the Treasury Department has met growth in its borrowing need by increasing the size of its weekly bill auctions, while maintaining the sizes of its seven monthly auctions of notes and bonds with maturities ranging from two to 30 years.
That will have to change eventually — or else risk bills growing as a share of the total debt, which exposes US taxpayers to rising interest rates because bills mature more frequently. Since early 2024, the Treasury's quarterly policy statements have said it expects to keep auction sizes steady "for at least the next several quarters." Bond market strategists expect that guidance to change when the next statement is made on Nov. 4.
(Corrects amount of previous record in second paragraph and new borrowing amount in third paragraph of story originally published on Oct. 30, before the release of the Treasury quarterly policy statement.)

item.title: Democratic Senate takeover halts Trump’s campaign to reshape the Fed OR Trump’s Fed pressure campaign hits a Democratic wall in the Senate
item.author: Jennifer Schonberger
item.description:
Democratic Senate takeover halts Trump’s campaign to reshape the Fed OR Trump’s Fed pressure campaign hits a Democratic wall in the Senate
2026-11-06
Por Jennifer Schonberger
https://finance.yahoo.com/economy/policy/article/trumps-fed-pressure-campaign-hits-a-new-democratic-wall-in-the-senate-100000283.html
Democrats secured control of the Senate on Tuesday, a seismic shift that effectively blocks President Trump's campaign to reshape the Federal Reserve and neutralizes what many analysts viewed as a threat to the central bank's independence.
It also heightens the challenge for Trump should he maneuver to replace any sitting officials.
"Democrats' control of the Senate reclaims the party's ability to approve or deny the President's nominees for judges and heads of other executive branch agencies," Jonathan Pingle, an economist for UBS, wrote in a note. "That includes the need for Democrats to approve any new members of the Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System should one of the existing governors step aside."
That political firewall directly impacts the administration's ongoing effort to remove Fed governor Lisa Cook. Trump fired Cook in August 2025, claiming she committed mortgage fraud by making misrepresentations on loan documents years before her appointment to the central bank. Cook, a Biden appointee, has denied any wrongdoing and sued. The lawsuit has gone through multiple court rungs before reaching the Supreme Court earlier this year.
Last month, Trump established a committee to determine whether her statements constituted legal "cause" for removal from the central bank, signaling that his efforts to oust her are continuing.
Read more: How much control does the president have over the Fed and interest rates?
However, Tuesday's election significantly changed the stakes of that investigation. Michael Feroli, chief US economist for JPMorgan, noted that the Senate flip alters the math for the White House.
"Even a successful removal would not open a seat up to a friend of the administration," Feroli wrote in a client note.
Jaret Seiberg, analyst with TD Cowen, agreed that the inability to confirm a replacement may make Trump less inclined to fire Cook.
Not everyone is convinced the administration will back down, however. Loretta Mester, former head of the Cleveland Fed, told Yahoo Finance, "Perhaps it makes it less likely he will succeed, but I'm not convinced it will stop the president from trying."
More broadly, Democrats taking power in Congress changes the atmosphere in which Fed officials work to set monetary policy devoid of political influence.
Trump has been vocal and persistent in urging policymakers to lower interest rates. The central bank has held steady, raising rates at times despite the White House pressure. The new power dynamic gives them more cover.

item.title: California's billionaire tax on track for defeat as the state continues to count votes
item.author: Ben Werschkul
item.description:
California's billionaire tax on track for defeat as the state continues to count votes
2026-11-06
Por Ben Werschkul
https://finance.yahoo.com/economy/article/californias-billionaire-tax-on-track-for-defeat-as-the-state-continues-to-count-votes-190840319.html
California's proposed billionaire tax appeared headed for defeat on Wednesday in one of the final verdicts from voters in an election week that saw a wave of anti-billionaire sentiment elsewhere.
The latest results on Wednesday afternoon showed California's Proposition 40 down by over 11 percentage points, with 60% of votes counted but the race not yet formally called.
The referendum would amend California's constitution and impose a one-time 5% tax on California residents and trusts with assets over $1 billion on Jan. 1, 2026. The revenue would primarily go toward healthcare, as well as food assistance and education.
Some assets, such as real property and certain retirement accounts and pensions, were excluded.
The measure was estimated to impact about 200 billionaires in the state. It faced fierce opposition from many in Big Tech and lost steam with voters as Election Day neared.
Google (GOOG, GOOGL) co-founder Sergey Brin was one of the measure's most vocal opponents. He contributed a reported $102 million to a political committee to fight the measure.
Other billionaires made detailed plans in case it passed. Meta (META) CEO Mark Zuckerberg told his board, according to a New York Times report, that they needed to take steps to shield him from the tax or he would publicly list his home in Palo Alto for sale.
The measure was also opposed by some Democrats, who argued it wouldn't work.
Outgoing California Gov. Gavin Newsom emerged as an opponent, arguing that billionaires would both dodge the tax and leave the state. He cited a report from the California Legislative Analyst's Office that estimated the measure might temporarily boost state revenues but could be an overall drag on regular income taxes and "would reduce state revenues by less than $1 billion per year."
Across the country, voters in red and blue states delivered verdicts on wealth inequality and the influence of the ultrarich. In Texas, where Elon Musk spent more than $200 million to keep the state's Senate seat in Republican hands, voters flipped the seat for Democrats and made clear their unease over AI data centers.
Tuesday's results also saw a series of wins by candidates who represent the Democratic Socialists of America, many of whom ran on explicitly anti-billionaire platforms. At least seven DSA members will take seats in Congress next year, as well as the mayors' offices of Los Angeles and Washington, D.C.
California voters were also weighing competing measures: Proposition 41 and Proposition 42, which were introduced by opponents of Proposition 40 to prevent the wealth tax from taking effect.

item.title: Higher memory prices taking a bite out of Apple’s margins
item.author: Daniel Howley
item.description:
Higher memory prices taking a bite out of Apple’s margins
2026-11-04
Por Daniel Howley
https://finance.yahoo.com/technology/article/higher-memory-prices-take-a-bite-out-of-apples-margins-161921051.html
Apple (AAPL) reported better-than-anticipated Q4 results after the bell on Friday, with iPhone and Services revenue topping Wall Street estimates.
But the company's stock fell after it told analysts on its earnings call that rising memory prices driven by the AI buildout will take a bigger bite out of margins going forward.
Apple stock fell more than 2% Tuesday.
While CFO Kevan Parekh said he expects Q1 to be Apple's best quarter ever, he also noted that gross margins will come in between 45% and 46%, down from 47.89% in Q4 and below the 48.16% the company saw in Q1 last year.
Parekh attributed the declines to higher memory costs and to the ramping up of Siri AI.
Complicating matters is the fact that Apple saw a roughly 1% margin benefit in Q4 from tariff refunds. The company also says it managed to offset higher memory costs in prior quarters thanks to carry-in inventory and lower prices on non-memory components.
But that powder is running dry.
"What we're seeing with memory pricing right now is unprecedented," CEO John Ternus said, later adding that the company increased its manufacturing purchase obligations by $33 billion from the June to September quarter.
The AI buildout isn't just hitting memory prices, though. It's also disrupting chip manufacturing more generally. Apple has repeatedly called out supply constraints related to advanced processing nodes for its high-powered chips.
That, coupled with less flexibility in the global supply chain, is impacting the company's ability to increase its inventory.
But as more of Apple's devices transition to newer processing nodes, that should begin to improve.
Still, the company expects supply constraints on its Mac and iPad lines in Q1 due to the memory crisis.
There's still no end in sight for the memory and storage, either. Companies like Micron (MU) and SK Hynix (SKHY) have said it will likely last until 2030, keeping the pressure on for far longer.

item.title: Why the Democrat blue wave could be a good thing for Apple stock
item.author: Brian Sozzi
item.description:
Why the Democrat blue wave could be a good thing for Apple stock
2026-11-04
Por Brian Sozzi
https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/article/why-the-democrat-blue-wave-could-be-a-good-thing-for-apple-stock-100051134.html
True to form, Wall Street is wasting no time picking winners and losers from the fresh Democratic blue wave that washed through the midterm elections late Wednesday.
One winner could be Apple for two reasons, opines EvercoreISI analyst Amit Daryanani.
The first is more of a defensive play amid the unknown that is fresh DC gridlock.
"Apple offers a different earnings driver through iPhone mix/pricing and services rather than data-center construction; our work points to resilient demand, with gross-margin recovery and price elasticity the key tests. This is THE name to keep working when investors want to get defensive," Daryanani says.
The other aspect is cooling memory chip prices, a major headwind for Apple, as data center projects get delayed or outright blocked by the Dems.
Said Daryanani, "Memory input inflation (DRAM & NAND) has been a sizable headwind for a host of names in our coverage (AAPL for example, talked about 140bps GM headwind in Dec-qtr due to memory, but also PC names). Could a slowdown in DC buildouts actually temper memory demand and, in a way, help companies that have been impacted by the sizable memory inflation (AAPL is the key one but there are many others)?"
Apple shares rose 0.5% in pre-market trading on Thursday.
The midterm election results threaten to significantly disrupt AI data center expansion as voter backlash over soaring utility bills, grid instability, and water usage drives a sharp political pivot toward tighter regulatory oversight.
In Texas, a dramatic political shift saw James Talarico capture a US Senate seat and Gina Hinojosa oust Greg Abbott in the gubernatorial race. This brings unprecedented scrutiny to ERCOT's independent grid allocations and unchecked tech consumption.
Paired with Senate wins by Roy Cooper in North Carolina and Sherrod Brown in Ohio, along with Amy Acton's win for governor there, these victories signal that the era of friction-free, subsidized hyperscaler build-outs could come to an abrupt end.
"Ohio, Texas and Georgia and that has implications for the AI trade and data center buildout. In the end – voters delivered a clear warning to the AI buildout: the money may be available, but local permission to build is becoming harder to secure and project delays can shift the timing of the spending but it does NOT eliminate the demand," said Slatestone Wealth chief market strategist Kenny Polcari.

item.content:encoded:
Why the Democrat blue wave could be a good thing for Apple stock

2026-11-04

Por Brian Sozzi

https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/article/why-the-democrat-blue-wave-could-be-a-good-thing-for-apple-stock-100051134.html

True to form, Wall Street is wasting no time picking winners and losers from the fresh Democratic blue wave that washed through the midterm elections late Wednesday.

One winner could be Apple for two reasons, opines EvercoreISI analyst Amit Daryanani.

The first is more of a defensive play amid the unknown that is fresh DC gridlock.

"Apple offers a different earnings driver through iPhone mix/pricing and services rather than data-center construction; our work points to resilient demand, with gross-margin recovery and price elasticity the key tests. This is THE name to keep working when investors want to get defensive," Daryanani says.

The other aspect is cooling memory chip prices, a major headwind for Apple, as data center projects get delayed or outright blocked by the Dems.

Said Daryanani, "Memory input inflation (DRAM & NAND) has been a sizable headwind for a host of names in our coverage (AAPL for example, talked about 140bps GM headwind in Dec-qtr due to memory, but also PC names). Could a slowdown in DC buildouts actually temper memory demand and, in a way, help companies that have been impacted by the sizable memory inflation (AAPL is the key one but there are many others)?"

Apple shares rose 0.5% in pre-market trading on Thursday.

The midterm election results threaten to significantly disrupt AI data center expansion as voter backlash over soaring utility bills, grid instability, and water usage drives a sharp political pivot toward tighter regulatory oversight.

In Texas, a dramatic political shift saw James Talarico capture a US Senate seat and Gina Hinojosa oust Greg Abbott in the gubernatorial race. This brings unprecedented scrutiny to ERCOT's independent grid allocations and unchecked tech consumption.

Paired with Senate wins by Roy Cooper in North Carolina and Sherrod Brown in Ohio, along with Amy Acton's win for governor there, these victories signal that the era of friction-free, subsidized hyperscaler build-outs could come to an abrupt end.

"Ohio, Texas and Georgia and that has implications for the AI trade and data center buildout. In the end – voters delivered a clear warning to the AI buildout: the money may be available, but local permission to build is becoming harder to secure and project delays can shift the timing of the spending but it does NOT eliminate the demand," said Slatestone Wealth chief market strategist Kenny Polcari.

Brian Sozzi is Yahoo Finance's Executive Editor, host of the Sozzi Unleashed morning show, the 'Power Players With Brian Sozzi' podcast and a member of Yahoo Finance's editorial leadership team.

item.title: Global financial markets were already fragile. Big AI bets could break them
item.author: Dhara Ranasinghe; Amanda Cooper
item.description:
Global financial markets were already fragile. Big AI bets could break them
2026-11-04
Por Dhara Ranasinghe; Amanda Cooper
https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/articles/analysis-global-markets-were-already-050846745.html
By Dhara Ranasinghe and Amanda Cooper
LONDON, Nov 3 (Reuters) - Financial markets are struggling under the weight of wars, soaring sovereign debt and trade tensions, with signs of trouble showing across the world — from the selloff in Japanese and French bonds to plunging emerging-market currencies. Now, the one trade that helped investors remain optimistic is starting to show cracks as well.
So far, the multitrillion-dollar spending splurge on artificial intelligence, aided by Washington's light-touch approach to business, has propelled stock markets to record highs and raised expectations for the global economy to grow a healthy 3% this year.
But investors are getting nervous about market resiliency. US President Donald Trump's erratic trade policies and the Iran war's energy shock have revived inflation worldwide, putting pressure on central banks to raise interest rates. That, along with AI's capital-investment surge and highly indebted governments, is driving up borrowing costs to multidecade highs.
With US midterm elections, volatile geopolitics and central bank policy promising further uncertainty in the final stretch of the year, some investors and economists say risks to the global economy are mounting.
"Rising rates always seem to sniff out and expose the most vulnerable time after time," said Jim O'Neill, former Goldman Sachs chief economist and former British Treasury minister. "Countries and businesses too exposed suffer the most."
He said if inflation did not ease, the risks stemming from the vast amount of debt-financed investment flowing into the AI sector would grow. The US central bank has missed its inflation target for more than half a decade; euro-area inflation at 3.8% is also above its 2% target.
"In some ways, it's surprising to me there haven't been more bumps in the AI trade already," O'Neill said.
'SIGNS OF THINGS BREAKING'
Market jitters showed up abruptly in October, when investors rushed out of AI stocks and into safe-haven bonds.
More than $2 trillion in market value was wiped from the tech-heavy Nasdaq 100 last month, as Big Tech's earnings intensified investor scrutiny of whether the cash invested can generate returns quickly enough. The cost of insuring bonds of some tech companies surged, some proposed data center projects struggled to raise money, and technology stocks from South Korea and China to the US tumbled.
Investors flocked to bonds. Yields, which move inversely to price, fell from multidecade highs, with the benchmark 10-year Treasury, which guides borrowing costs globally, falling almost 20 basis points on October 22, its biggest daily fall since early 2023.
The 10-year yield is still hovering around 5%, a threshold some investors see as a risk to broader financial stability.
Strains were already showing up in parts of the world where the AI buildout has been less of a driving force.
In France, bond yields soared to levels last seen during the 2012 euro zone debt crisis, leaving the government with little room to address demands from protesters who have taken to the streets in the worst civil unrest in years.
In Japan, whose economy is dependent on energy imports, bond yields recently hit 30-year peaks. Authorities are under pressure to raise rates faster, undermining Tokyo's policy goals that called for additional spending and possibly upending global capital flows.
"There are some signs of things breaking," said Mike Riddell, a lead portfolio manager at Fidelity International, which manages over $1 trillion worth of assets, pointing to troubles in France and Australia, where the housing market is in the throes of the worst downturn in decades.
German bonds, also considered a safe haven, have become more attractive, Riddell added.
US econ
[Transcripcion recortada]

item.title: SpaceX, Tesla stocks sink as analyst warns Democrats' victory will create 'major hurdles' for AI build-out
item.author: Ines Ferré
item.description:
SpaceX, Tesla stocks sink as analyst warns Democrats' victory will create 'major hurdles' for AI build-out
2026-11-04
Por Ines Ferré
https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/article/spacex-tesla-stocks-sink-as-analyst-warns-democrats-victory-will-create-major-hurdles-for-ai-build-out-135511616.html
SpaceX, Tesla stocks sink as analyst warns Democrats' victory will create 'major hurdles' for AI build-out
One of Wall Street's biggest AI bulls says the sweeping Democratic victory in the midterm elections will slow the pace of the AI data center build-out in the US over the next two years.
AI-related stocks dropped on Wednesday, including Elon Musk-led SpaceX (SPCX) and EV maker Tesla (TSLA), which fell 4% in early trading. Shares of cloud provider CoreWeave (CRWV) and data center-related companies IREN (IREN) and Vertiv (VRT) also traded lower on Wednesday after Democrats won a majority in the House and Senate on Tuesday night and flipped governorships across key states.
"There is no way to sugarcoat that Democrats taking control, especially over the Senate, will create some major hurdles for AI and tech legislation in the Beltway over the next 2 years," Yorkville's partner and managing director, Dan Ives, wrote on Wednesday.
Those hurdles, Ives said, will slow the pace of 800 to 1,000 planned AI data centers across the US. The analyst pointed out that the biggest worry for tech investors and the AI trade is the state of Texas, where around 25%-30% of data center gigawatts and capacity will come from.
Democrat Gina Hinojosa won the Texas Governor race over incumbent Greg Abbott in a surprise result. While Abbott currently has a moratorium on data centers in Texas, the prevailing view was that it would have ended were he reelected.
"Hinojosa is a known anti-data center politician and negative on the AI buildout, which makes worries around the future of the data center buildout in Texas a real issue for tech investors," Ives said.
Tesla and SpaceX caught 'in this spiderweb'
This poses a problem for companies like Texas-based SpaceX, which has been building out its AI infrastructure and taking steps toward a potential merger with Tesla.
"SpaceX and Musk are clearly caught front and center in this spiderweb," said Ives.
"There will be a lot of negotiations and politics on this front especially in Texas which is the foundation of the AI buildout in the US … and Big Tech will need to embrace this new political landscape as of today," he added.
"Data centers in space looking pretty appealing right now," Elon Musk wrote on X following the election results.
Data center concerns emerged as a key issue in the 2026 midterm elections, with candidates facing growing public opposition to proposed facility locations, the expansion of power infrastructure needed to support them, and concerns that rising electricity demand could drive up consumer costs.
One silver lining for investors may be that political headwinds will force a slowdown in AI capex. AI-related jitters have already weighed on the tech (XLK) sector in recent weeks, with financing concerns hitting neocloud providers that rent out computing capacity, while semiconductor stocks have also retreated.

item.title: Oil prices ease to settle near 4-week low on hopes peace talks will end wars
item.author: Scott DiSavino
item.description:
Oil prices ease to settle near 4-week low on hopes peace talks will end wars
2026-11-04
Por Scott DiSavino
https://finance.yahoo.com/energy/articles/oil-rises-report-us-strike-012715191.html
By Scott DiSavino
NEW YORK, Nov 3 (Reuters) - Oil prices eased about 1% on Tuesday to the lowest in nearly four weeks, as the market weighed talks to end the wars in Ukraine and Iran against worries that recent attacks in both conflicts could further disrupt supplies.
The world is also watching US midterm elections to see whether President Donald Trump's Republican Party can retain control of the US Congress for the rest of his second term. Opinion polls and nonpartisan analysts expect Democrats to wrest the House of Representatives, while the Senate remains uncertain.
Brent futures fell $1.17, or 1%, to settle at $103.60 a barrel, their lowest close since October 7. US West Texas Intermediate crude fell 37 cents to settle at $96.09, its lowest since October 14.
Iran and the US are still far from a deal to end their war, a senior Iranian official told Reuters, while mediator Qatar stepped up efforts to avert an escalation after the US midterm elections.
Qatar's Foreign Ministry spokesperson said the US and Iran remain committed to mediation efforts and are reviewing proposals aimed at bridging their differences.
"Despite these positive signals, it's probably too early to think escalation risks have passed," ING said in a note. "What is clear, though, is that strong signals of progress in peace talks would mean more downside for prices."
Overnight, the US carried out strikes on Iran's Qeshm Island. A US official said the strikes targeted surface-to-air missiles used against US assets. Another official said the strikes appeared limited and did not signal a return to major combat operations.
Separately, Trump said he made a deal with Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu that Washington would stop $4 billion in funding to Israel after the end of this year.
Saudi state oil company Aramco is working to expand a crude pipeline that circumvents the Strait of Hormuz, CEO Amin Nasser said.
The effective blockade of the chokepoint that links the Gulf to world markets, previously a conduit for 20% of global oil supplies, has redrawn energy flows and infrastructure investment priorities among the region's oil producers.
RUSSIA AND UKRAINE
Russia will hold three-way peace talks with Ukraine and the US in Abu Dhabi from November 10 to 11, the Kremlin confirmed.
Russia was the world's third-biggest crude oil producer behind the US and Saudi Arabia in 2025, US energy data showed. Sanctions designed to keep Russian energy out of global markets after Moscow's invasion of Ukraine have helped support oil prices.

Iran and the US are still far from a deal to end their war, a senior Iranian official told Reuters, while mediator Qatar stepped up efforts to avert an escalation after the US midterm elections.
Qatar's Foreign Ministry spokesperson said the US and Iran remain committed to mediation efforts and are reviewing proposals aimed at bridging their differences.
"Despite these positive signals, it's probably too early to think escalation risks have passed," ING said in a note. "What is clear, though, is that strong signals of progress in peace talks would mean more downside for prices."
Overnight, the US carried out strikes on Iran's Qeshm Island. A US official said the strikes targeted surface-to-air missiles used against US assets. Another official said the strikes appeared limited and did not signal a return to major combat operations.
Separately, Trump said he made a deal with Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu that Washington would stop $4 billion in funding to Israel after the end of this year.
Saudi state oil company Aramco is working to expand a crude pipeline that circumvents the Strait of Hormuz, CEO Amin Nasser said.
The effective blockade of the chokepoint that links the Gulf to world markets, previously a conduit for 20% of global oil supplies, has redrawn energy flows and infrastructure investment priorities among the region's oil producers.
RUSSIA AND UKRAINE
Russia will hold three-way peace talks with Ukraine and the US in Abu Dhabi from November 10 to 11, the Kremlin confirmed.
Russia was the world's third-biggest crude oil producer behind the US and Saudi Arabia in 2025, US energy data showed. Sanctions designed to keep Russian energy out of global markets after Moscow's invasion of Ukraine have helped support oil prices.

item.title: Copper, Tin Fall With Base Metals on Renewed AI Stocks Selloff
item.author: Bloomberg News
item.description:
Copper, Tin Fall With Base Metals on Renewed AI Stocks Selloff
2026-11-04
Por Bloomberg News
https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/commodities/articles/copper-tin-fall-metals-renewed-025516249.html
(Bloomberg) -- Copper and tin fell with other industrial metals, as a renewed selloff in technology stocks in Asia weakened the demand outlook for materials used in data centers and to solder circuit boards.
Most Read from Bloomberg
Both contracts dropped more than 1% on the London Metal Exchange as concerns persisted over spending and stretched valuations at artificial intelligence companies. Tin has plunged 10% this quarter, the worst performer among the LME's six major metals.
Copper had risen on Monday, helped in part by a pullback in oil prices that could mitigate inflation pressures. The US and Iran have signaled a willingness to pursue peace talks, easing anxiety over the war's impact on interest rates and global growth.
Still, macro conditions are putting a lot of pressure on metals, particularly given the possibility that the conflict could resume after the US midterm elections, said Xu Wanqiu, an analyst with Cofco Futures Co.
Copper fell 1.2% to $14,180 a ton as of 10:50 a.m. in Shanghai, while tin declined 2.2% to $48,550 a ton. Aluminum dropped 1.1% to $3,060.50 a ton.
Most Read from Bloomberg Businessweek
2026 Bloomberg L.P.

item.title: Job openings and hiring edged higher in September, but it's still a 'low hire, low fire' market
item.author: Claire Boston
item.description:
Job openings and hiring edged higher in September, but it's still a 'low hire, low fire' market
2026-11-04
Por Claire Boston
https://finance.yahoo.com/economy/article/job-openings-and-hiring-edged-higher-in-september-but-its-still-a-low-hire-low-fire-market-151812343.html
Job openings and hiring changed little in September, the Labor Department's monthly Job Openings and Labor Turnover Survey showed, as the "low hire, low fire" labor market continued.
There were 7.5 million job openings in September, from a revised 7.2 million a month earlier, the report showed. The hiring rate improved slightly to 3.4%, up from 3.3% in September.
Read more: How jobs, inflation, and the Fed are all related
Layoffs were also little changed at 1.6 million, with 1% of workers losing their jobs. Voluntary quits ticked up slightly to 3.4 million, and the rate of quits rose slightly to 2.1%, from 1.9% in August.
The latest data suggest a continuation of a long labor market trend of slow hiring, but minimal layoffs. A fuller look at the job market will be released on Friday, when the Bureau of Labor Statistics publishes its monthly payrolls report for October. Economists surveyed by Bloomberg expect the US to have added 65,000 jobs last month.
Claire Boston is a senior reporter for Yahoo Finance covering housing, mortgages, and home insurance.

item.title: The economy is 'less K-shaped than you think' — and that's bad news for the Fed
item.author: Jared Blikre
item.description:
The economy is 'less K-shaped than you think' — and that's bad news for the Fed
2026-11-04
Por Jared Blikre
https://finance.yahoo.com/economy/article/the-economy-is-less-k-shaped-than-you-think--and-thats-bad-news-for-the-fed-110000449.html
Americans at every income level are richer than they were before the pandemic.
That's good news for households and a headache for a Fed that has watched inflation, excluding food and energy, run above its target for more than five years.
Picture the letter K. In a K-shaped economy, the top arm shoots up while the bottom arm slides down.
Apollo chief economist Torsten Sløk says the bottom arm is holding up better than most people think. "New data from the Fed shows that the US consumer is less K-shaped than commonly perceived," he wrote in an Oct. 31 note, pointing to spending growth of about 4% to 5% a year for every income group since 2024. (Disclosure: Yahoo is a portfolio company of funds managed by affiliates of Apollo Global Management.)
The Fed's wealth data backs him up. Household net worth is up more than 70% for every income group since early 2019, by Yahoo Finance calculations, including about 73% for the lowest-earning fifth and 85% for the top 1%.
Now count the dollars.
Of the nearly $84 trillion in new household wealth, the top 20% of earners collected about $63 trillion, or three-quarters. The bottom 20% got about $2 trillion.
Kyla Scanlon, author of "In This Economy?", explained on Yahoo Finance's Market Hang Monday why the economy can look strong even when most people don't feel it. Citing University of Michigan survey director Joanne Hsu, she said, "Spending is one dollar, one vote, whereas sentiment is one person, one vote."
The dollars keep voting at the cash register, and that's the Fed's problem.
A consumer this healthy keeps inflation sticky
"Core PCE inflation is supposed to be 2%," Sløk wrote in a Nov. 1 note. "Unfortunately, it has been 3% for three years, and it is now moving higher."
Core PCE, the Fed's favorite inflation gauge, rose 3.1% in September from a year earlier and hasn't dipped to 2% since early 2021. Sløk estimated last week that about half of that inflation now comes from strong demand, the part higher interest rates can actually help cool down.
Read more: How jobs, inflation, and the Fed are all related
So how much cooling would it take? A lot. His model says the Fed would need to lift its benchmark rate to roughly 6.75% by the end of 2027, he wrote in a Nov. 2 note. That's nearly 3 percentage points above today's 3.75%-4% range and would be the highest since January 1991.
The Fed "may be further from its inflation goal than the market currently expects," Sløk wrote.
The next clue arrives with Friday's October jobs report, which will show whether hiring is still strong enough to keep a December rate hike on the table. And since the top of the K owns the most stock, a lasting AI sell-off could cool the big spenders faster than any rate hike.

item.title: Prediction markets give Republicans slightly better odds of holding the Senate. They’re more aligned with pollsters regarding the House.
item.author: Ben Werschkul
item.description:
Prediction markets give Republicans slightly better odds of holding the Senate. They’re more aligned with pollsters regarding the House.
2026-11-04
Por Ben Werschkul
https://finance.yahoo.com/economy/article/prediction-markets-vs-polls-election-forecasting-industry-faces-midterm-test-100000463.html
Prediction markets and pollsters both say Democrats are favored to take both the US House and Senate in the midterms. Prediction markets have been a little less certain about it, though traders' odds jumped on Tuesday on the chances of Democrats taking control of the Senate.
That's setting up what could be another chapter in the burgeoning rivalry between prediction markets and polls following 2024's closely watched results.
The differences have been most evident in the upper chamber. A small but consistent gap has been evident for months in the odds of Democrats winning control of the Senate. The gap has averaged about 7.3 percentage points since Sept. 1, according to a Yahoo Finance analysis.
But the gap has narrowed approaching Election Day, closing to 2.9 percentage points on Tuesday morning. Three prediction markets place a 77.3% chance of Democrats taking control, while two polling-based models put the chances a bit higher at 80.2%.
The odds have been a bit more evenly matched around the House of Representatives, with an average gap of less than a percentage point in recent months.
The latest read on Tuesday showed a 2.2-percentage-point gap, with prediction markets suggesting a 94% chance of Democrats flipping the chamber, versus 96.2% odds from polls.
This analysis was conducted by averaging the daily odds from three leading prediction markets, Kalshi, Polymarket, and PredictIt, to create one rolling prediction market measure. Those values were then compared to the average of two leading poll-focused models — one from statistician Nate Silver and another from Harvard called ElectIt.
These gaps have had an outsized effect on public perceptions in recent years.
This was especially true in 2024, when a 10-percentage-point difference between prediction markets and polls led to some post-election analyses claiming that prediction markets had gotten the results right and polls had gotten them wrong.
The stakes for prediction market companies are high. Kalshi and Polymarket have long argued that their markets are more truthful than polls because market participants have money on the line. The markets also had a high-profile miss recently when the winner of Brazil's presidential election was given just 20% odds before ultimately prevailing.
The scrutiny also comes as these markets continue to grow rapidly. Kalshi shared new data over the weekend that more than $1.2 billion has now been traded on midterm markets, surpassing the platform's volume during the 2024 presidential election.
Increased government scrutiny of the prediction markets
Policymakers, meanwhile, have ramped up criticism of the sector and promised challenges on both the legislative and legal fronts.
Senator Elizabeth Warren, who could lead the Senate's powerful banking committee if Democrats take power, and Republican Senator John Curtis teamed up on a recent letter to both Kalshi and Polymarket raising concerns about election-related prediction markets and possible market manipulation.
"We are particularly troubled by election-related event contracts," the senators wrote. "Event contracts tied to elections receive prominent coverage and are treated by some observers as indicators of political momentum."
In Curtis's home state of Utah, a lawsuit brought by Kalshi is challenging whether federal rules can overrule Utah's anti-gambling laws, which lawmakers want to apply to prediction markets.
In an amicus brief supporting Utah, the group Better Markets wrote, "the stakes couldn't be higher ... Utah has every right to decide that Utahns shouldn't be subjected to sports betting's harms."
A gap that proved significant in 2024
There are also echoes th
[Transcripcion recortada]

item.title: Binance founder Changpeng Zhao addresses historic crypto hack: 'There's no 100% security'
item.author: Brian Sozzi
item.description:
Binance founder Changpeng Zhao addresses historic crypto hack: 'There's no 100% security'
2026-11-04
Por Brian Sozzi
https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/crypto/article/binance-founder-changpeng-zhao-addresses-historic-crypto-hack-theres-no-100-security-123427760.html
It has been a busy few days for Changpeng Zhao in the wake of the hack on the enormous crypto platform he co-founded, Binance.
"It's been a pretty hectic process," Zhao, better known in crypto circles as CZ, told Yahoo Finance. "But the good thing is right now the withdrawals have been restored, the systems back to normal. People are free to use the platform without any issues now. And then all user funds are covered. The users did not suffer any loss."
Binance is the world's largest cryptocurrency trading platform and holds approximately $171 billion in total assets on its platform. The company is led by co-CEOs Richard Teng and Yi Le.
Hackers recently drained roughly $6.3 billion worth of digital assets from Binance on Oct. 29.
$6.3 billion Binance hack shakes crypto industry
Here's what you need to know:
Blockchain intelligence firms and the FBI attributed the 20-minute raid with high confidence to TraderTraitor, an elite state-sponsored cyber unit tied to North Korea.
North Korea reportedly denied involvement.
Rather than cracking private cryptographic keys, the attackers reportedly breached internal automated transaction workflows via a Binance employee's laptop.
Read more: How to keep your crypto safe
Binance moved swiftly to stabilize the situation by guaranteeing full customer restitution, deploying corporate treasury reserves, Secure Asset Fund for Users (SAFU) capital, and insurance funds to replenish user balances.

Binance is the world's largest cryptocurrency trading platform and holds approximately $171 billion in total assets on its platform. The company is led by co-CEOs Richard Teng and Yi Le.

Hackers recently drained roughly $6.3 billion worth of digital assets from Binance on Oct. 29.

$6.3 billion Binance hack shakes crypto industry

Here's what you need to know:

Blockchain intelligence firms and the FBI attributed the 20-minute raid with high confidence to TraderTraitor, an elite state-sponsored cyber unit tied to North Korea.

North Korea reportedly denied involvement.

Rather than cracking private cryptographic keys, the attackers reportedly breached internal automated transaction workflows via a Binance employee's laptop.

Read more: How to keep your crypto safe

Binance moved swiftly to stabilize the situation by guaranteeing full customer restitution, deploying corporate treasury reserves, Secure Asset Fund for Users (SAFU) capital, and insurance funds to replenish user balances.

"There's no 100% security," CZ added. "So when you run a platform, especially a crypto platform the possibility is always there. I did not think it was going to be this big of magnitude, probably not."

item.title: These 3 sectors could be in focus next year in Washington — no matter who wins on Tuesday
item.author: Ben Werschkul
item.description:
These 3 sectors could be in focus next year in Washington — no matter who wins on Tuesday
2026-11-04
Por Ben Werschkul
https://finance.yahoo.com/economy/article/these-3-sectors-could-be-in-focus-next-year-in-washington--no-matter-who-wins-on-tuesday-173922303.html
The 2026 campaign has featured bipartisan calls for action on pharmaceuticals, the housing market, and AI data centers, a sign that this trio of sectors may be in focus in Washington no matter which party prevails on Tuesday.
The critical comments are especially notable coming from Republicans as the campaign enters its final days. Democratic rhetoric about reining in big business is nothing new, but the GOP's focus indicates both an increased willingness within the party to adopt a populist stance and a potential openness to strike deals next year in the new power-sharing landscape.
And the high likelihood that Democrats will win control of at least one chamber of Congress could elevate these issues — with or without President Trump's support.
Democrats are now strongly favored to win a majority in the House, with a Harvard election forecasting model pegging the odds on Friday at 94%. The Senate is less clear, but its 60-vote threshold means any action next year there will require bipartisan buy-in.
That is always a heavy lift in today's increasingly polarized Washington, but the housing issue provided proof of concept this year, after a major piece of legislation passed and became law despite Trump's refusal to sign it.
The coming year is likely to feature "meaningful opportunities and risks for key sectors," Stifel chief Washington policy strategist Brian Gardner wrote in a recent note to clients.
He suggested tech companies and data center operators will face challenging headlines, but "risks are low that Congress would pass heavy-handed legislation ... we expect that it would enact a light-touch framework."
He added that the healthcare sector could be in closer focus, writing "a change in power on Capitol Hill could be seen as a negative for pharmaceuticals as Democrats and the White House might agree to further regulate drug prices."
Pharmaceuticals are a prime example of this dynamic, with a high volume of campaign-trail rhetoric coming from both parties.
GOP Senate hopeful Mike Rogers of Michigan cut an ad saying "the pharmaceutical companies are ripping American families off," while Iowa Republican Ashley Hinson is pledging to "put the squeeze on Big Pharma."
That means — regardless of whether Rogers, Hinson, or their Democratic opponents win next Tuesday — openly critical lawmakers will head to Washington amid prominent areas of bipartisan agreement on regulating drug companies.
One dramatic and notable bill, titled the Break Up Big Medicine Act, would take aim at vertical integration in the healthcare system. It is being pushed by two lawmakers who agree on little else: Republican Josh Hawley and Democrat Elizabeth Warren.
Calls to rein in data centers that 'could plausibly spook markets'
Data centers are another issue that has unified many in both parties.
There is a range of calls for action — from a moratorium on new construction to new taxes on these companies — with Republican candidates in high-profile Senate races making notable pivots.
Republican Sen. Jon Husted of Ohio is in the midst of a close reelection campaign and has been pushing a bill that would require companies to pay for the energy infrastructure needed to support new data centers.
The question of government action on data centers is also extending to races for governor, with states able to enact their own restrictions.
Henrietta Treyz and Dan McCarthy of Veda Partners wrote in a recent note to clients that "the 2026 gubernatorial elections could materially change the regulatory outlook for planned data center projects in several states."
Perhaps the race most in focus is Texas's governor's race between Republican incumbent Greg Abbott and Democratic challenger Gin
[Transcripcion recortada]

item.title: Chip stocks are bouncing back from a fresh bear market as Wall Street’s safe havens slip
item.author: Jared Blikre
item.description:
Chip stocks are bouncing back from a fresh bear market as Wall Street’s safe havens slip
2026-11-04
Por Jared Blikre
https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/article/chip-stocks-are-bouncing-back-from-a-fresh-bear-market-as-wall-streets-safe-havens-slip-152637092.html
Monday's close left chip stocks in a fresh bear market, below their summer lows and a key technical level. Tuesday, they're bouncing back like they want to make the bears regret it.
The PHLX Semiconductor Index (^SOX) finished Nov. 2 about 22% below its Oct. 6 high, its second bear market since June. It was also the index's second straight close below its 200-day moving average, a line it hadn't closed under since June 2025, and its lowest close since April.
Nearly every chip and storage stock in the S&P 500 rose in early trading Tuesday, led by memory and chip-equipment names, and the index climbed back above its July 29 low. If chips can hold that ground, Monday's breakdown starts to look like a bear trap — a break below a key level that quickly reverses, catching traders who bet on more losses.
The bigger hurdle sits just overhead. The iShares Semiconductor ETF (SOXX) needs to get back above its 200-day average, near $477, to start repairing the damage. Above that, the next levels to watch are about $524 and $596.
The calendar is on the bulls' side
Chip stocks have climbed in all eight midterm cycles since 1994, measured from the last October close through the following June, by Yahoo Finance calculations. That's the stretch Stock Trader's Almanac editor Jeff Hirsch calls the best months of the year for semiconductors. But in 2002 and 2018, chips first fell about another 11% before the rally kicked in.
Election Day itself has been kind to stocks too. The S&P 500 (^GSPC) has risen on 10 of the last 14 midterm election days, going back to 1970.
Meanwhile, the rest of the market is moving the other way. Roughly two-thirds of S&P 500 stocks fell in early trading, a mirror image of Monday, when about 7 in 10 rose while chips sank. Consumer staples, utilities, and real estate, the safe havens that carried the market through October, slipped.
From the Oct. 6 close through Nov. 2, staples and health care climbed about 10% to 11%, while SOXX fell 23%.
Apple (AAPL), which has become Wall Street's hedge against the AI trade, saw its shares fall after it warned that memory costs will keep rising. Luke Kawa, head of markets at Sherwood News, called the seesaw between Apple and chips "almost Pavlovian."
"Apple goes down and what goes up in response? Semis," Kawa told Yahoo Finance on Nov. 3.
He also sees real damage in the charts. "What seems different this time is that it's really the first time throughout the AI boom that we're now seeing … lower highs and lower lows across major swaths of the space," Kawa said. Lower highs and lower lows are the very definition of a downtrend.

item.title: CrowdStrike announces 'kill switch' for AI agents that go rogue
item.author: Ines Ferré
item.description:
CrowdStrike announces 'kill switch' for AI agents that go rogue
2026-11-04
Por Ines Ferré
https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/article/crowdstrike-says-it-will-buy-2-ai-cybersecurity-startups-announces-kill-switch-for-ai-agents-163631619.html
What happened: CrowdStrike (CRWD) announced a 'kill switch' for AI agents, sending its shares up more than 1% on Tuesday. The cybersecurity company also agreed to buy two AI security startups. The combined purchase price for both is $495 million, according to the Wall Street Journal.
What's behind the move: CrowdStrike said it developed a 'Kill Switch' in Falcon Guardian, giving security teams control over AI agents. If an agent deviates from its intended behavior, a defender can terminate it wherever it runs, prevent it from launching again, and cut off its access to the enterprise network.
"AI safety is how you get the full benefit of AI. When you deploy agents with a kill switch, you stay in control," said George Kurtz, CEO and founder of CrowdStrike, in a press release.
CrowdStrike stock rose 1% before the bell on Wednesday.
What else you need to know: CrowdStrike also announced on Tuesday that it has signed an agreement to acquire Fiddler AI, a startup that develops tools that help companies track their AI systems.
The company also announced an agreement to acquire Dreadnode, a startup that develops tools to test AI systems for security vulnerabilities. CrowdStrike said the technology will enable its Falcon platform to continuously scan AI models, applications, and agents for potential security weaknesses before deployment.
Despite concerns earlier this year that AI would disrupt traditional business models, cybersecurity companies have instead benefited from the rise of agentic AI, which is driving increased demand for verification and authentication.

item.title: Supermicro tops Q1 estimates, offers strong Q2 outlook
item.author: Daniel Howley
item.description:
Supermicro tops Q1 estimates, offers strong Q2 outlook
2026-11-04
Por Daniel Howley
https://finance.yahoo.com/technology/article/supermicro-tops-q1-estimates-offers-strong-q2-outlook-220213885.html
Data center infrastructure company Supermicro (SMCI) reported its fiscal first quarter earnings after the bell on Tuesday, beating Wall Street's expectations on the top and bottom lines and providing a better-than-anticipated outlook for Q2.
The company said it anticipates Q2 sales of between $19.5 billion and $21.5 billion. Analysts were calling for $16.35 billion.
Supermicro stock edged slightly higher before the bell on Wednesday.
"Supermicro's transformation into a Total AI and IT Datacenter Solution provider continues to accelerate, delivering record revenue of $19.9 billion for the first quarter fiscal 2027," CEO Charles Liang said in a statement.
"[Data Center Building Block Solutions] is driving significant value for our customers — from gigawatt-scale data centers down to single-container PODs — which, including our expanding software, proactive service, and networking solutions, is enhancing profitability and long-term shareholder value. Through key enterprise partnerships and expanding global production capacity, we are making AI infrastructure faster to deploy, with superior uptime and more cost-effective for our customer base."
For the quarter, the company reported earnings per share (EPS) of $1.81 and revenue of $19.95 billion, well ahead of Wall Street's projections and the company's preliminary results.
Gross margins topped 12.8%, also topping Supermicro's preliminary numbers of between 12% and 12.5%.
Supermicro stock fell a staggering 27% over the last month after Gartner issued a report saying that 80% of neocloud companies would cease operations by 2030 due to a lack of a return on invested capital.
Neoclouds CoreWeave (CRWV) and Nebius (NBIS) plunged on the news and are down 40% and 37%, respectively, in the last month. CoreWeave is a Supermicro customer.
Supermicro stock has had a rough year, plummeting 38% over the last 12 months on questions about its profitability.

"[Data Center Building Block Solutions] is driving significant value for our customers — from gigawatt-scale data centers down to single-container PODs — which, including our expanding software, proactive service, and networking solutions, is enhancing profitability and long-term shareholder value. Through key enterprise partnerships and expanding global production capacity, we are making AI infrastructure faster to deploy, with superior uptime and more cost-effective for our customer base."

For the quarter, the company reported earnings per share (EPS) of $1.81 and revenue of $19.95 billion, well ahead of Wall Street's projections and the company's preliminary results.

Gross margins topped 12.8%, also topping Supermicro's preliminary numbers of between 12% and 12.5%.

Supermicro stock fell a staggering 27% over the last month after Gartner issued a report saying that 80% of neocloud companies would cease operations by 2030 due to a lack of a return on invested capital.

Neoclouds CoreWeave (CRWV) and Nebius (NBIS) plunged on the news and are down 40% and 37%, respectively, in the last month. CoreWeave is a Supermicro customer.

Supermicro stock has had a rough year, plummeting 38% over the last 12 months on questions about its profitability.

item.title: AMD beats Q3 earnings expectations, with data center revenue climbing 97%
item.author: Daniel Howley
item.description:
AMD beats Q3 earnings expectations, with data center revenue climbing 97%
2026-11-04
Por Daniel Howley
https://finance.yahoo.com/technology/article/amd-beats-q3-earnings-expectations-with-data-center-revenue-climbing-97-125553256.html
AMD (AMD) reported its third quarter results after the bell on Tuesday, beating expectations on the top and bottom lines, as the company's data center revenue grew 97%.
"Demand for our Instinct and EPYC products continued to strengthen, and we expect growth to accelerate further in the fourth quarter as we scale Helios and 'Venice' production," CEO Lisa Su said in a statement.
"With our leadership product portfolio and deep customer and supply chain relationships, we are confident in our ability to sustain very strong revenue growth and expanding profitability over the coming years."
For the quarter, AMD saw earnings per share (EPS) of $2.09 on revenue of $13.38 billion. Analysts were projecting EPS of $1.97 on revenue of $13.08 billion, according to Bloomberg consensus estimates.
The company saw EPS and revenue of $1.20 and $9.2 billion, respectively, in the same period last year.
AMD's Data Center arm generated sales of $8.5 billion, ahead of estimates of $8.19 billion. It reported revenue of $4.34 billion in the same period last year.
Last month, the company announced its Helion reference design, a server rack designed to be outfitted with various configurations of AMD's CPUs and GPUs based on customers' needs.
AMD's Client business revenue, which includes PC sales, hit $2.9 billion. Wall Street was looking for $3.06 billion.
The chipmaker's gaming business sales, however, came in at $773 million, down 40% year over year. Analysts were estimating revenue of $655 million.
The company's gaming division includes products ranging from PC graphics cards to custom silicon for game consoles. Both categories are facing higher prices due to the ongoing memory and storage shortage, depressing customer demand.
AMD's report comes after rival Intel reported better-than-anticipated Q3 results, but issued guidance well below analysts' projections last week. The news sent Intel stock plummeting nearly 29%.
The company blamed the outlook on a worse-than-anticipated decline in the PC market.
The industry is contending with two overlapping factors: difficult comparisons to last year, when Microsoft ended support for Windows 10, forcing enterprises to purchase newer Windows 11 systems, and the steady increase in PC prices, which is eating into demand.

item.title: Robinhood in ‘Food Fight’ for Anthropic IPO Retail Allocation
item.author: Paige Smith
item.description:
Robinhood in ‘Food Fight’ for Anthropic IPO Retail Allocation
2026-11-03
Por Paige Smith
https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/articles/robinhood-food-fight-anthropic-ipo-195640332.html
(Bloomberg) -- Robinhood Markets Inc. is competing with other retail brokerages to fight for access to Anthropic PBC's mega-IPO.
Most Read from Bloomberg
The firm fields demand from its clients for access to shares in an initial public offering, then sends it to the company going public and the banks handling the stock sale, Robinhood Chief Financial Officer Shiv Verma said Monday in a Bloomberg Television interview.
"It's a food fight out there, so we're going to let our demand speak for itself, and then let the companies decide," Verma said.
When SpaceX went public in June, all eligible customers putting in requests for shares with platforms run by Robinhood and competitors Charles Schwab Corp., Fidelity Investments, SoFi Technologies Inc. and Morgan Stanley's E*Trade were allocated some stock. Leading up to the event, the firms jockeyed for a greater allocation, given that retail clients are often at a disadvantage in accessing pre-IPO companies.
Verma said that SpaceX wanted to allocate around 15% to 20% to retail investors, while Robinhood set aside 20% of is own shares for such clients during its own IPO.
"What we are making sure the companies know is, retail is here, they are a force to stay, and given they're 20% to 25% of the equities market, they should consider a large allocation to retail," Verma said.
Anthropic, maker of the Claude chatbot, filed on Oct. 26 for an IPO slated to occur before the US Thanksgiving holiday later this month. The company disclosed Monday that it plans to spend more than $895 billion in the years ahead.
--With assistance from Tim Stenovec and Carol Massar.
Most Read from Bloomberg Businessweek
2026 Bloomberg L.P.

item.title: Estée Lauder CEO on surging fragrance sales: 'Consumers are getting younger'
item.author: Brian Sozzi
item.description:
Estée Lauder CEO on surging fragrance sales: 'Consumers are getting younger'
2026-11-03
Por Brian Sozzi
https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/article/estee-lauder-ceo-on-surging-fragrance-sales-consumers-are-getting-younger-130714358.html
Tom Ford owner Estée Lauder (EL) has seen a boom in fragrance sales.
Fragrance net sales increased 20% in the company's fiscal first quarter, Estée Lauder reported on Monday. It was one of the fastest-growing divisions for the company in the quarter.
Gains were fueled by double-digit growth in high-end brands Le Labo, Tom Ford, Jo Malone London, and Kilian Paris. Estée Lauder also notched growth.
"Tom Ford is getting younger and younger as a brand," Estee Lauder CEO Stéphane de La Faverie told Yahoo Finance on a media call. "What is interesting with the consumer trend, I would say, is not specific to Tom Ford but … like broad-based on fragrance, is consumers are getting younger around the world."
He added, "But in the case of fragrance, you're seeing a group of young consumers, boys and girls, that are really, you know, buying fragrances with different habits. Like, if I look at me, for instance, I grew up with a signature fragrance, one that was defining who I was. This young generation is really tailoring their fragrance portfolio based on occasion. Can be to go to school, for sports, to go on a date, or to go with their parents and things like that."
The performance helped to drive a better-than-expected quarter and outlook.
Organic sales are poised to grow by 4% to 5.5% in the current fiscal year. Estée Lauder previously estimated 3% to 5%.
The company lifted its full-year earnings outlook by 10 cents.
Shares rose more than 1% in premarket trading.

item.title: White House’s Hassett Dismisses Concern Over Financing of AI
item.author: Christopher Anstey
item.description:
White House’s Hassett Dismisses Concern Over Financing of AI
2026-11-03
Por Christopher Anstey
https://finance.yahoo.com/technology/ai/articles/white-house-hassett-dismisses-concern-133942048.html
(Bloomberg) -- White House National Economic Council Director Kevin Hassett dismissed concerns about financing of the artificial intelligence build-out, saying there is plenty of capital in the system for such funding.
Most Read from Bloomberg
"It's actually like a really well-financed ecosystem," Hassett said of AI in an interview Monday on CNBC. He was responding to a question about last week's tumble in technology shares, which sent the Nasdaq Composite index to the lowest since July.
Hassett said that it's true that "some companies that maybe have a lot of debt, and you kind of worry about" that. But "there are really, really big-pocketed companies sort of lurking all over the place, owning the equity, owning the debt, perhaps willing to pounce if somebody has trouble."
"There's so much cash in the ecosystem that I think that people should be reassured" even after last week's drop in stocks, he said. "Sometimes things need to go down a little bit" after a big run-up, he said of markets. "But I don't think that there's a risk of a wholesale selloff at all."
Most Read from Bloomberg Businessweek
2026 Bloomberg L.P.

item.title: Anthropic's IPO day will test the AI trade. But what happens next matters more.
item.author: Brian Sozzi
item.description:
Anthropic's IPO day will test the AI trade. But what happens next matters more.
2026-11-03
Por Brian Sozzi
https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/article/anthropics-ipo-day-will-test-the-ai-trade-but-what-happens-next-matters-more-184038893.html
The response in the days and weeks after Anthropic's (ANTH.PVT) looming initial public offering will be more important to the broader AI ecosystem than the IPO itself, according to former longtime Cisco (CSCO) CEO and JC2 Ventures founder John Chambers.
"I think more important than what [the stock] comes out at is, after the IPO is out, do we see steady gains in terms of this stock and therefore encouraging others to go public and follow forward on it?" Chambers said on Sozzi Unleashed.
Given the rising concerns about the health of the AI ecosystem, it's a coin flip as to how Anthropic's debut on public markets will go — and what the days after will look like.
The model builder did little to quiet down concerns on Monday. In an amended S-1 filing, Anthropic said that third quarter sales rose 1,127% to $17 billion. But revenue growth slowed on a quarter-over-quarter basis.
Third quarter sales increased 47% compared with a 144% growth rate in the second quarter. Sales increased 132% in the first quarter.
The company lost a staggering $23.29 billion in the third quarter.
Investment bankers are reportedly aiming for an astronomical listing valuation of roughly $1.5 trillion to $2 trillion.
Anthropic could debut on public markets before the end of November. It plans to list on the Nasdaq under the ticker symbol ANT.
"The position of Anthropic in terms of long-term leadership is extremely strong," Chambers added.

Anthropic could debut on public markets before the end of November. It plans to list on the Nasdaq under the ticker symbol ANT.
"The position of Anthropic in terms of long-term leadership is extremely strong," Chambers added.

item.title: Marvell to purchase Lumentum for $115 billion in record-breaking AI tech deal, both stocks tank
item.author: Ines Ferré
item.description:
Marvell to purchase Lumentum for $115 billion in record-breaking AI tech deal, both stocks tank
2026-11-03
Por Ines Ferré
https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/article/marvell-to-purchase-lumentum-in-115-billion-deal-as-ai-124702761.html
What happened: Marvell Technology (MRVL) shares fell more than 10% on Monday after the chip designer announced it will acquire optical component maker Lumentum (LITE) in a deal valued at $115 billion. The transaction would be the largest merger between two publicly traded companies on record. Lumentum shares also fell 15% following the announcement.
What's behind the move: Lumentum stock tanked following the announcement as the deal's all-stock structure leaves investors exposed to Marvell's recent sell-off. Under the agreement, Lumentum shareholders will receive 4.5 shares of Marvell common stock for each share owned.
While that exchange ratio initially implied a valuation of $1,132 per share based on Oct. 28 prices, Marvell's recent drop has steadily eroded the payout's actual value.
The record-breaking agreement is expected to expand the combined company's total addressable market to $550 billion, according to the announcement.
"AI infrastructure is undergoing a fundamental architectural shift toward optical connectivity, creating an opportunity that comes along once in a generation," Matt Murphy, chairman and CEO of Marvell, said on Monday.
Read more about trending tech stock moves and today's market action.
What else you need to know: The acquisition gives Marvell greater access to optical technologies and manufacturing capacity, which have become critical bottlenecks of the AI infrastructure build-out.
Lumentum makes lasers and other optical components as increasingly powerful AI systems require faster connections. Marvell, which competes with Broadcom (AVGO), designs high-speed infrastructure and custom chips that enable AI computers to communicate with one another.
Earlier this year, Marvell stock rallied sharply after AI chip heavyweight Nvidia (NVDA) CEO Jensen Huang described the chip designer as "the next trillion-dollar company."
The company joined the S&P 500 (^GSPC) index in June. Marvell shares are up more than 120% year to date. Lumentum shares have rallied more than 100%.
