item.title: Musk is throttling Grok because its cost is 'unsustainably high'
item.author: Hamza Shaban
item.description:
Musk is throttling Grok because its cost is 'unsustainably high'
2026-11-03
Por Hamza Shaban
https://finance.yahoo.com/technology/article/musk-is-throttling-grok-because-its-cost-is-unsustainably-high-162959909.html
Elon Musk said on Sunday that Grok (SPCX) users would run up against usage limits more quickly than normal because servicing Grok Bot has become too expensive.
"The cost of serving Grok Bot was unsustainably high relative to revenue," Musk wrote on his social media platform, X.
The sudden throttling highlights one of the biggest questions swirling around the AI revolution: whether demand from users will be enough to sustain a business. It turns out, at least in Musk's case, that demand isn't the problem. The cost is.
Musk was responding to an X user complaining that their Grok Bot usage jumped to 100% before their reset date, when typically they never reached their cap while using the AI agent.
User demand is just one side of the AI market equation, and the businesses churning out sophisticated and expensive models have to — or will have to, eventually — generate revenue to cover their heightened costs. The economics of the still-new and messy AI industry suggest that even healthy demand can't always sustain the AI tools they're selling. Not at these prices — for the users (cheap) and for the corporate compute (expensive; just look at the computing bills).
That's why the revenue question is increasingly critical and why Musk's admission is so significant. The AI business is running into real-world limitations.
Musk suddenly changing Grok subscriptions so that the AI-usage meter runs faster has struck users and tech observers as unfair and worrisome for SpaceX's business.
"Two weeks ago Grok Bot was an incredible success story powering SpaceXai's revenue growth. Now it's unsustainable and loses money (???)", wrote former xAI worker Benjamin De Kraker in a post on X. Other commenters pointed to a bold and now ironic post Musk sent out a few days ago, saying, "Saving money for the distant future is pointless with the advent of super intelligent abundance."
The tenor of the comments on Musk's own platform, filled with Grok users, turned noticeably sharp: "Yet another Elon rug-pull."
Musk, as he does, is posting through it.
"Just being sensible," he wrote on X, in response to a comment suggesting that investors would punish SpaceX for the decision. In fact, shares are up 5% on Monday. And why shouldn't they be? Wall Street has always loved fiscal responsibility and capitalizing on demand.
Another way to think through the change is that Musk was simply offering an introductory rate to hook users.
Perhaps AI subscriptions are going through their own version of the "VC subsidy," popularized when Uber, Lyft, and other venture-backed apps offered discounts and super-low rates to boost adoption and engagement, only for the apps to sharply increase prices once users became reliant on the services. The classic introductory rate strategy.
Grok, a user might ask, is that true?

item.title: US market correction nearing end, Morgan Stanley strategists say
item.author: Reuters
item.description:
US market correction nearing end, Morgan Stanley strategists say
2026-11-03
Por Reuters
https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/articles/us-market-correction-nearing-end-144736206.html
Nov 2 (Reuters) - The US market correction that began in June is in its "final innings", Morgan Stanley strategists said on Monday, adding that the November 3 midterm elections should help remove a major market overhang.
"We expect near-term clearing events to provide an attractive opportunity to add risk to quality cyclicals that have de-rated as we head into 2027," strategists led by Michael Wilson, Morgan Stanley's chief US equity strategist, said.
• The S&P 500 is catching down to weaker market breadth, which is typically the last stage of a slump, Wilson said, noting 60% of Russell 3000 stocks have already seen at least a 20% correction since June
• The risk of a correction led by AI company earnings has kept markets on the edge. Last month, the tech-heavy Nasdaq-100 shed trillions of dollars in market value and was on the brink of entering correction territory
• Large-cap stocks have typically gained 15% in the six months following election results, they said, adding that a Democratic sweep is already priced-in by investors
• The bigger risk would be what comes after the vote, with the potential of renewed military escalation with Iran or new tariffs, Morgan Stanley said
• Recent earnings reinforce signs that the market correction could be nearing its end
• "Investors are no longer overlooking FCF shortfalls as they often did earlier in the cycle, consistent with a more typical mid- to late cycle environment where earnings durability and cash conversion matter more," Wilson said
• He does not expect the Federal Reserve to rush toward interest rate cuts or add support, relief could come from the US Treasury spending down its cash pile, from about $1.05 trillion to about $850 billion by year-end
(Reporting by Kanchana Chakravarty in Bengaluru; Editing by Tasim Zahid)

item.title: Why investors are dumping tech stocks, in one image
item.author: Brian Sozzi
item.description:
Why investors are dumping tech stocks, in one image
2026-11-03
Por Brian Sozzi
https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/article/why-investors-are-dumping-tech-stocks-in-one-image-123636288.html
Tech stocks aren't getting shredded for any old reason. It's actually very fundamental: Free cash flow is drying up for Big Tech leaders, and capex is rising dramatically.
Investors are questioning whether this ratio is totally out of whack, given more realistic growth projections for AI.
The combined capex of Amazon, Alphabet, Meta and Microsoft rose by $36.9 billion in the third quarter to $201.9 billion, the team at The Kobeissi Letter calculated (chart below). This figure has more than doubled over the past 12 months, and is up a staggering 356% since the first quarter of 2024.
Big Tech has now spent $1.6 trillion on capex over the last three years, the strategists say.
At the same time, the combined free cash flow of these companies fell $33.1 billion last quarter to a negative $26.4 billion, its lowest on record.
Free cash flow among these tech beasts has fallen by $88.2 billion over the last year.
Only Microsoft reported positive free cash flow in the third quarter.
Looking ahead, the strategists estimate these four companies plan to spend another $232 billion on capex in the fourth quarter.
The AI trade saw a serious slamming on Friday, with more than $1 trillion in market value wiped away as investors fretted about the weakening cash flow profiles of Big Tech.
"The AI narrative is cracking as profitability concerns intensify," warned Miller Tabak chief markets strategist Matt Maley.

item.title: Anthropic reveals amended S-1 outlining huge spending commitments, rising sales
item.author: Daniel Howley
item.description:
Anthropic reveals amended S-1 outlining huge spending commitments, rising sales
2026-11-03
Por Daniel Howley
https://finance.yahoo.com/technology/article/anthropic-reveals-amended-s-1-outlining-huge-spending-commitments-rising-sales-153635825.html
Anthropic (ANTH.PVT) released an amended S-1 investor prospectus on Monday, updating its total revenue and spending through the first nine months of the year, showing increased sales and massive spending numbers.
The company said revenue grew $1,206% to $33.2 billion through the first nine months of the year that ended Sept. 30.
The original S-1, which covered the first six months of the year through June 30, listed revenue of $16.3 billion. Anthropic recorded revenue of $4.6 billion in all of 2025.
Operating losses also improved year over year to -$1.3 billion in the first nine months of 2026 from -$5.2 billion in the same period in 2025.
Anthropic reported an operating loss of $536 million in the September quarter, compared with operating income of $974 million in the June quarter.
The company says the decline is the result of a $5 billion charge for compute under short-term commitments, as well as $2 billion in non-cash charges from its donation matching program.
The AI giant also revealed a staggering aggregate committed spend of $895.4 billion, which it says is primarily related to compute and infrastructure. Some $447.5 billion of that will hit before Dec. 31, 2030, with the remainder coming between 2031 and 2045; $69.8 billion will be due over the next 12 months.
The company's market debut will test investors' appetite for a second public listing by a firm with an already massive valuation. SpaceX (SPCX) went public on June 12 at $150 per share and ended the day 20% higher.
Anthropic didn't appear to make many changes to its vast risks section, which outlines possible scenarios in which the company's AI could go out of control, causing damage that even the world's combined insurance industry may not be able to cover.
In an early September essay, CEO Dario Amodei called on the AI industry to slow the development of frontier AI models over fears that they could become too powerful for humans to control. The piece, coupled with statements by former and current researchers at AI companies, sent shockwaves through the industry and raised concerns that the technology could "kill all humans."
Experts dispute those claims, saying that the risks surrounding AI stem from basic cybersecurity protections and from preventing people and governments from using it for things like identity theft, discrimination, and labor displacement.
Correction: Anthropic's revenue grew 1,206% over the first nine months of the year. A previous version of this article misstated the growth as 1,026%.

item.itunes:summary:
Anthropic reveals amended S-1 outlining huge spending commitments, rising sales
2026-11-03
Por Daniel Howley
https://finance.yahoo.com/technology/article/anthropic-reveals-amended-s-1-outlining-huge-spending-commitments-rising-sales-153635825.html
Anthropic (ANTH.PVT) released an amended S-1 investor prospectus on Monday, updating its total revenue and spending through the first nine months of the year, showing increased sales and massive spending numbers.
The company said revenue grew $1,206% to $33.2 billion through the first nine months of the year that ended Sept. 30.
The original S-1, which covered the first six months of the year through June 30, listed revenue of $16.3 billion. Anthropic recorded revenue of $4.6 billion in all of 2025.
Operating losses also improved year over year to -$1.3 billion in the first nine months of 2026 from -$5.2 billion in the same period in 2025.
Anthropic reported an operating loss of $536 million in the September quarter, compared with operating income of $974 million in the June quarter.
The company says the decline is the result of a $5 billion charge for compute under short-term commitments, as well as $2 billion in non-cash charges from its donation matching program.
The AI giant also revealed a staggering aggregate committed spend of $895.4 billion, which it says is primarily related to compute and infrastructure. Some $447.5 billion of that will hit before Dec. 31, 2030, with the remainder coming between 2031 and 2045; $69.8 billion will be due over the next 12 months.
The company's market debut will test investors' appetite for a second public listing by a firm with an already massive valuation. SpaceX (SPCX) went public on June 12 at $150 per share and ended the day 20% higher.
Anthropic didn't appear to make many changes to its vast risks section, which outlines possible scenarios in which the company's AI could go out of control, causing damage that even the world's combined insurance industry may not be able to cover.
In an early September essay, CEO Dario Amodei called on the AI industry to slow the development of frontier AI models over fears that they could become too powerful for humans to control. The piece, coupled with statements by former and current researchers at AI companies, sent shockwaves through the industry and raised concerns that the technology could "kill all humans."
Experts dispute those claims, saying that the risks surrounding AI stem from basic cybersecurity protections and from preventing people and governments from using it for things like identity theft, discrimination, and labor displacement.

item.title: Palantir beats Q3 estimates, raises full-year revenue outlook as US commercial sales accelerate
item.author: Ines Ferré
item.description:
Palantir beats Q3 estimates, raises full-year revenue outlook as US commercial sales accelerate
2026-11-03
Por Ines Ferré
https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/article/palantir-beats-q3-estimates-raises-full-year-revenue-outlook-as-us-commercial-sales-top-us-government-revenue-for-the-first-time-234245540.html
Palantir (PLTR) beat Wall Street estimates on its third quarter revenue and profit on Monday and raised its full-year revenue outlook as the data software company's US commercial business surpassed its US government sales for the first time ever.
Shares of Palantir were volatile, falling 6% during premarket hours on Tuesday.
Palantir reported Q3 revenue of $2.313 billion, a 96% increase from the previous year. Wall Street had expected revenue of $2.17 billion, according to Bloomberg data.
Palantir now sees full-year revenue between $8.530 billion and $8.534 billion, topping analyst estimates of $8.2 billion. The company also raised its US commercial sales target to more than $3.559 billion. Adjusted earnings per share of $0.44 also beat consensus estimates of $0.40.
As for the company's explosive business, Palantir CEO Alex Karp said during the earnings call, "We've gone from being the most attractive person in the physics department to being the captain of the football team."
What else you need to know: Palantir stock is up roughly 2% year to date, even as the company has been caught in the recent tech sell-off. The stock weathered headwinds earlier this year after fears of AI disruption hit the entire software complex.
Palantir has frequently pushed back on those concerns, arguing that the enterprise AI market is splitting into two camps: companies paying millions of dollars for model tokens only to receive "AI slop," and those using the company's underlying infrastructure layer.
Palantir's commercial business has accelerated sharply, building on momentum from its historically dominant US government base.
Earlier this year, Palantir's Maven Smart System became an official Pentagon program, cementing a multiyear role across US military AI projects
Wall Street is mostly bullish on the stock, with 30 Buy ratings, nine Holds, two Sells, and a consensus price target of $216 per share.

item.title: Oil prices slide as hopes rise for potential US-Iran diplomatic breakthrough
item.author: Jake Conley
item.description:
Oil prices slide as hopes rise for potential US-Iran diplomatic breakthrough
2026-11-03
Por Jake Conley
https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/commodities/article/oil-prices-slide-as-hopes-rise-for-potential-us-iran-diplomatic-breakthrough-182732084.html
Oil prices took a leg down on Monday as the outlook for potential diplomatic breakthroughs in the Middle East strengthened just a day before midterm elections that could represent a pivotal moment for the Iran war.
Futures on Brent crude (BZ=F), the international benchmark, shed around 7.9% to trade below $105 per barrel, while those on US WTI crude (CL=F) lost 7.5% to hold near $96.
Oil futures initially began to move downward on Monday after Axios reported that, while Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu has pressed the White House for a forceful round of strikes on Iran, President Trump has said he wants to give diplomacy with Tehran another shot.
The reporting from Axios aligns with public statements in recent days from President Trump, where he has said the US won't strike Iran after the midterms. However, reporting by national outlets in recent weeks has indicated that the US military has briefed Trump on options for a major reescalation after the midterms, when the risk of political backlash against the president will be lessened.
Read more: How oil price shocks ripple through your wallet, from gas to groceries
Adding to the downward pressure on oil prices Monday, leaders in Tehran said contact with the US over negotiations to end the war is continuing, Reuters reported, as talks between Iran and Qatari mediators have produced proposal language but no breakthrough agreement.
"Consultations through mediators are very intensive," Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said in comments to the state-run media outlet IRNA. "We have presented our conditions and proposals and everything depends on the political rationality of Washington."
Leaders in China and Russia both spoke out against a full-fledged resumption of hostilities on Monday, in comments from their foreign ministries. China is a major buyer of energy from the Gulf region, and after largely staying out of the conflict through its first several months, it has engaged more directly in recent weeks.
In Russia, the war in Iran has added to the nation's domestic fuel shortage, caused largely by strikes on oil refineries by the Ukrainian military and international sanctions levied against Moscow. President Vladimir Putin reportedly spoke with Iranian security lead official Mohsen Rezaei on Monday , per Reuters.
Even so, the diplomatic headlines haven't yet tempered predictions on Wall Street that oil prices will remain higher for longer. Goldman Sachs analysts led by Daan Struyven said on Monday that they now expect Brent prices to average $105 per barrel in December, up from a previous forecast of $90. They see Brent contracts averaging $88 per barrel in 2027, up from a prior $80 forecast.

item.title: ‘More and more disenchanted’: A final check-in on Trump’s economic approval ratings before Tuesday’s election
item.author: Ben Werschkul
item.description:
‘More and more disenchanted’: A final check-in on Trump’s economic approval ratings before Tuesday’s election
2026-11-03
Por Ben Werschkul
https://finance.yahoo.com/economy/article/more-and-more-disenchanted-a-final-check-in-on-trumps-economic-approval-ratings-before-midterms-100000424.html
President Trump's economic approval ratings are hovering at second-term lows, with inflation worries the central headwind for the president and his party as the midterm elections loom.
A raft of recent polls underscores this reality: Trump's low overall approval ratings are being dragged down by economic sentiment that is even lower.
A new national poll released on Sunday by NBC News found that a majority of Republicans — 53% — say they are dissatisfied with the state of the economy.
And inflation remains the top-of-mind issue, with only about 25.3% of voters approving of Trump's handling of inflation versus 69.5% who disapprove, according to an average of recent polls calculated on Sunday by forecaster Nate Silver.
Another tabulation from RealClearPolitics this past weekend showed a 70.4% disapproval rating of the president's handling of prices, which voters often say is their top issue.
Deep voter dissatisfaction is evident on other financial issues like tariffs and taxes. The president is facing a negative net rating of -29.7% on trade and -31.1% on the economy overall, according to Silver, with this economic drag outpacing Trump's overall net approval rating of -22.6%.
As Ipsos summarized their results this past week, "American consumers have grown more and more disenchanted with the economy and the Trump administration," noting that disapproval of Trump's handling of the economy has nearly doubled since his inauguration and remains the No. 1 issue for voters.
"All that spells trouble for Republicans across the nation on Tuesday," the pollsters concluded.
Economic dissatisfaction with both Trump and his party
Democrats, meanwhile, are hitting new highs ahead of the election even as voters often give the opposition party mixed marks overall.
Those results are being fueled by respondents who listed inflation as their top issue. In a Focaldata-Financial Times poll this past week, 47% of respondents said Democrats would do a better job handling that issue versus 34% who said the same about Republicans.
One possible glimmer of hope for Republicans in that data: 20% of voters say they are either unsure or that neither party would do a better job.
The data for the GOP has become so challenging that some results show voters are inclined to dismiss Republicans' record on taxes, an issue that historically has been a strength and a centerpiece of Trump's economic agenda over the last two years.
"I signed the Great Big Beautiful Bill, delivering the largest tax cuts in American history, including no tax on tips, no tax on overtime, no tax on Social Security," the president said Thursday in South Carolina.

item.title: Disney Eyes Thousands of Layoffs, With Managers Asked to Cut 20%
item.author: Thomas Buckley
item.description:
Disney Eyes Thousands of Layoffs, With Managers Asked to Cut 20%
2026-11-02
Por Thomas Buckley
https://finance.yahoo.com/media-advertising/articles/disney-eyes-thousands-layoffs-managers-002025007.html
(Bloomberg) -- Walt Disney Co. is moving toward thousands of job cuts with the entertainment giant asking some managers to target 20% in annual cost savings, according to people familiar with the matter.
Most Read from Bloomberg
The savings could come from job eliminations as well as from expense reductions, said the people, who asked to not be identified because the discussions are private.
Some of Disney's operations, which range from theme parks, TV network and the movie studio, will be affected disproportionately. Chief Executive Officer Josh D'Amaro aims to reinvest a portion of the savings into film and TV programming, technology and the theme parks and cruise ship businesses, the people said.
The company has promised double-digit growth in adjusted earnings per share in the current fiscal year.
A representative for Disney declined to comment.
Disney has cut billions of dollars worth of costs and eliminated thousands of positions in recent years, with reductions impacting every division including ABC, Pixar, ESPN, the film studio and the experiences unit. The company had 231,000 people worldwide at the end of the last fiscal year.
The Wall Street Journal reported on Oct. 1 that Disney was planning a restructuring of its TV division, and cuts at the company's legal and global affairs unit.
Other entertainment companies including Netflix Inc., Sony Pictures Entertainment and Skydance Corp.'s Paramount and Warner Bros. divisions have also cut jobs as revenue from traditional television declines and streaming subscriber growth slows. The also have to cope with more viewers tuning to social media, online videos and streaming services backed by tech giants like Amazon.com Inc. and Apple Inc.
At the Bloomberg Screentime conference in Los Angeles last month, Disney President Dana Walden said that "there is a need to constantly evaluate how you're structured and how big is the organization. Technology set their sights on our business and we must survive and thrive and grow, and that's what we're going to do."
Most Read from Bloomberg Businessweek
2026 Bloomberg L.P.

The also have to cope with more viewers tuning to social media, online videos and streaming services backed by tech giants like Amazon.com Inc. and Apple Inc.
At the Bloomberg Screentime conference in Los Angeles last month, Disney President Dana Walden said that "there is a need to constantly evaluate how you're structured and how big is the organization. Technology set their sights on our business and we must survive and thrive and grow, and that's what we're going to do."

item.title: Gas prices likely to drop below $4 a gallon in the next week if oil prices keep declining, analyst says
item.author: Ines Ferré
item.description:
Gas prices likely to drop below $4 a gallon in the next week if oil prices keep declining, analyst says
2026-11-02
Por Ines Ferré
https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/article/gasoline-could-fall-below-4-in-the-next-week-as-oil-prices-drop-says-analyst-171201913.html
Gas prices likely to drop below $4 a gallon in the next week if oil prices keep declining, analyst says
Gasoline prices are on track to fall below the $ 4-per-gallon threshold if the Middle East conflict doesn't escalate further and oil prices continue to decline, according to one industry analyst.
On Monday, the national average for gasoline was $4.16 per gallon, about $0.14 lower than a week ago and roughly $0.23 lower than a month ago, according to AAA data.
Over the weekend, US Secretary of State Marco Rubio signaled that President Trump favors negotiations over further attacks on Iran. The country's supreme leader also indicated that Tehran is open to talks, sending oil prices down more than 6%. Brent crude (BZ=F) fell to near $105 per barrel. West Texas Intermediate crude (CL=F) fell to around $97.
"The national average could fall under $4 a gallon in the next week barring a course change," Patrick De Haan, head of petroleum research at GasBuddy, wrote on X on Monday.
The analyst also noted more refining capacity could creep in the months ahead, adding a few thousand barrels per day, or even 10,000 barrels per day.
The move lower marks a reversal of the recent reacceleration in fuel costs as Middle East tensions escalated and inclement weather and constrained refining capacity put upward pressure on prices.
President Trump has said he will not attack Iran before the midterms and has suggested that fuel prices will decline afterward.
Read more: What an extended war with Iran could mean for gas prices
Last month, The New York Times reported that the US and Israel had reportedly drawn up plans for renewed attacks on Iran following the Nov. 3 elections. Around that time, the US also ordered nonessential embassy personnel to depart Saudi Arabia following a series of attacks targeting the country's airports and oil fields.
On Sunday night, Goldman Sachs analysts raised their Brent crude forecast to $105 per barrel for December, up from $90 previously. The analysts expect Brent to average $88 per barrel next year, up from an earlier forecast of $80 per barrel.

item.title: The Intel stock collapse is getting worse — and the $3.5Tchip rout is spreading
item.author: Jared Blikre
item.description:
The Intel stock collapse is getting worse — and the $3.5Tchip rout is spreading
2026-11-02
Por Jared Blikre
https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/article/the-intel-stock-collapse-is-getting-worse--and-the-37-trillion-chip-rout-is-spreading-212154947.html
Wall Street mostly swept up last week's tech wreckage Monday. Chip stocks kept tracking mud back through the house.
About 7 in 10 S&P 500 stocks rose Monday, yet nearly every chip stock fell, and the group shed more than $400 billion in market value in a single session, by Yahoo Finance calculations.
Intel (INTC) led the way down again.
The chipmaker slid about 9% after its worst day since 1974 on Oct. 30, when a disappointing forecast knocked nearly 29% off the stock. Monday's close left Intel worth less than half of what it was when September ended.
And the damage didn't stick to Intel.
Micron (MU), Sandisk (SNDK), Seagate (STX), and Western Digital (WDC) — the memory and storage names that led the chip boom this year — all got clobbered, falling roughly 6% to 8%. Marvell (MRVL) fell even harder, a drop that came as it agreed to buy Lumentum (LITE) in a $115 billion deal. Nvidia (NVDA) held up better than most, but it's still down about 16% since Oct. 6.
Zoom out and the mess gets bigger. Chip and memory stocks have lost about $3.7 trillion in market value since Oct. 6, by Yahoo Finance calculations. Nvidia lost the most in dollars, but Intel's drop of nearly half is the steepest among the giants.
Not everything tied to AI bled. SpaceX (SPCX) rose, though it's still well below where it started October. Software was mixed, apart from cybersecurity stocks like Fortinet (FTNT) and CrowdStrike (CRWD), which fell with chips.
Adam Johnson, founder of the Bullseye Brief and portfolio manager of the American Ingenuity Fund, thinks last week's sell-off already priced in the worst.
"The market kitchen-sinked it," Johnson told Yahoo Finance on Monday. "They discounted everything that could go wrong. And when you do that, typically that's when you see a bottom."
John Chambers, founder and CEO of JC2 Ventures and Cisco's former CEO, expects the gap between winners and losers to keep widening.
"There will be major train wrecks," Chambers told Yahoo Finance, also on Monday. "And rising tide does not raise all boats. I would not bet against Nvidia."
Stock Trader's Almanac editor Jeff Hirsch, who coined the term "Octoberphobia," bought the sell-off on Oct. 30. History is on his side. Chips have climbed in all eight midterm cycles since 1994, measured from the last October close through the following June, by Yahoo Finance calculations. But in 2002 and 2018, they first fell about another 11%.
Next up is AMD (AMD), which reports third quarter results Tuesday after the bell, the same day as the midterm vote.

item.title: Amazon is on a course to spend half a trillion dollars in a single year: JPMorgan
item.author: Brian Sozzi
item.description:
Amazon is on a course to spend half a trillion dollars in a single year: JPMorgan
2026-11-02
Por Brian Sozzi
https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/article/amazon-is-on-a-course-to-spend-half-a-trillion-dollars-in-a-single-year-jpmorgan-163113505.html
Amazon's (AMZN) big spending on AI investments is only just beginning, JPMorgan tech analyst Doug Anmuth warns.
"We do not expect capex growth to decelerate or slow next year, and as such we project capex of $395 billion in 2027 (+77% year over year) followed by $476 billion in 2028 (+20% year over year)," Anmuth wrote in a new note.
Amazon CEO Andy Jassy said last week the company would spend "meaningfully more" on capex in 2027, without providing a number. The company estimated its capex would hit $220 billion in 2026.
Anmuth added, "We believe management's strong visibility into demand gives it the confidence to underwrite 40%+ growth over the next two years and to invest even more aggressively in AI compute infrastructure."
The large checks Amazon cut to build out its AI infrastructure caught up with it in the third quarter.
Amazon's free cash flow decreased to an outflow of $42.4 billion for the trailing 12 months, driven primarily by a year-over-year increase of $94.8 billion in purchases of property and equipment. This increase primarily reflects investments in artificial intelligence, Amazon said.
This compares to a free cash flow inflow of $14.8 billion for the trailing 12 months ended Sept. 30 of last year.
Investors headed for the exit on Amazon stock post-earnings. Shares were down over 1% on Friday, but they bounced back Monday, taking the stock's year-to-date advance to 9%. The S&P 500 is up 11% on the year.
"Meaningfully more" now has a number next to it, thanks to Anmuth. A very, very large number.

item.title: Private Equity Is Boosting Republicans Over Democrats in Midterms
item.author: Dawn Lim; Allison McNeely; Bill Allison
item.description:
Private Equity Is Boosting Republicans Over Democrats in Midterms
2026-11-02
Por Dawn Lim; Allison McNeely; Bill Allison
https://finance.yahoo.com/economy/policy/articles/private-equity-boosting-republicans-over-111000873.html
(Bloomberg) -- The investing industry is throwing its weight behind Republican allies ahead of the US midterm elections in an effort to stem a populist wave it fears will bring greater scrutiny of private equity's reach.
Most Read from Bloomberg
Private equity and money managers doled out more donations to Republicans than Democrats this year for the first time since 2016, with billionaires from Apollo Global Management Inc. and Blackstone Inc. opening their checkbooks. Blackstone's chief executive and Republican mega-donor Steve Schwarzman has donated more than $33 million to Republican candidates and their allies this cycle.
Overall, donations to Republican candidates, leadership political action committees and party committees from the investing sector were nearly 70% higher than comparable contributions supporting Democrats, according to OpenSecrets data.
That disparity in giving is far wider than has been seen in recent election cycles. But this year the industry has seen a rightward tilt amid concerns that Democrats could regain control of the House of Representatives – and maybe the Senate, too – and turn the spotlight on an industry that progressives have often cast as a bogeyman. The hope is to boost allies that could block regulation and serve as legislative brakes under Democratic control.
While they put dollars behind Republicans, credit executives have also stepped up visits to influential Democrats in recent months, said a person familiar with the matter. That includes meeting with Representative Maxine Waters, the person said, the ranking member on the House Financial Services Committee who is likely to take a bigger oversight role if the Democrats control the chamber.
Executives are not only girding for an unfavorable legislative agenda: They worry that the industry is poised for a moment like big bank CEOs faced in the wake of the 2008 financial crisis, when executives were hauled in front of Congress for grilling. That kind of unwanted attention would be another headache for an industry already struggling with high interest rates, waning investor enthusiasm and underwhelming returns – and could come from a wide range of lawmakers.
"The industry views the populist streak on the right as just as worrying as the energy behind the progressive left," said James Maloney, managing partner of public affairs firm Tiger Hill Partners and a former spokesman for the industry's main lobby group.
As some take the view that both parties have strayed too far from the center, wealthy donors have favored moderate establishment Republicans. Schwarzman and his number-two executive Jon Gray, a longtime Democratic donor, are among those who have written checks to back Republican Senator Susan Collins' reelection bid in Maine.
She has threatened but ultimately supported dealmakers' ability to pay lower taxes on carried interest, or the slice of profits that private equity managers take on winning bets. Collins is in a tight race with Democrat Troy Jackson, a fifth-generation logger and former state lawmaker who has championed tougher rules on private equity.
Jackson has pointed fingers at the industry for the rising prices of houses, apartments and mobile homes. "I do think we have to go after private equity, make it so that they can't buy these things and charge outrageous prices," he said in an October debate.
Collins and an affiliated political action committee have hit back with an advertising blitz. Pine Tree Results PAC has raised more than $30 million through Oct. 14, according to Federal Election Commission data. Of all the PACs focused on a single candidate, it scored the most money from the private equity and investing industry — nearly $4 million, according to OpenSecrets. Top billio
[Transcripcion recortada]

item.title: US Awards Last of Trump’s Massive Strategic Oil Reserve Drawdown
item.author: Ari Natter; Lucia Kassai
item.description:
US Awards Last of Trump’s Massive Strategic Oil Reserve Drawdown
2026-11-02
Por Ari Natter; Lucia Kassai
https://finance.yahoo.com/energy/articles/us-awards-last-trump-massive-142945451.html
(Bloomberg) -- The Trump administration awarded contracts for nearly 41 million barrels from the nation's emergency oil reserve, completing a massive oil exchange aimed at curbing soaring energy prices after the war with Iran.
Most Read from Bloomberg
Trafigura Trading LLC and ExxonMobil Holdings Corp., were among the winners, according to the Energy Department. The sale marks the last of a 172 million-barrel emergency release from the Strategic Petroleum Reserve, the second-largest in its history. The release was the US contribution to a broader International Energy Agency plan to put 400 million barrels onto global markets.
The US has released a total of 174.1 million barrels since the war started, exceeding its initial 172 million-barrel pledge made with the IEA.
Crude, gasoline, diesel and jet fuel prices have surged since military operations against Iran began on Feb. 28, intensifying pressure on President Donald Trump to address rising fuel costs ahead of November's midterm elections, which could determine control of the House and Senate.
Still, Energy Secretary Chris Wright has signaled another drawdown from the reserve is unlikely. "I think the releases will spill into January and soon after that, you'll see the refill start," Wright said in an interview earlier this week.
The SPR has already fallen to its lowest level since 1982, in part because former President Joe Biden's administration withdrew roughly 290 million barrels from the system through a series of releases, including after Russia's invasion of Ukraine.
Because the release was structured as an exchange, essentially a loan that companies must repay with interest, the Energy Department has said the reserve will ultimately be replenished with about 200 million barrels, or roughly 20% more than what was released, over the next year.
Most Read from Bloomberg Businessweek
2026 Bloomberg L.P.

item.title: AI Policy Fears Grip Stock, Bond Traders With Midterms Days Away
item.author: Matthew Griffin; Victor Swezey; Felice Maranz
item.description:
AI Policy Fears Grip Stock, Bond Traders With Midterms Days Away
2026-11-02
Por Matthew Griffin; Victor Swezey; Felice Maranz
https://finance.yahoo.com/technology/ai/articles/ai-policy-fears-grip-stock-110000621.html
(Bloomberg) -- Wall Street expects Democrats to win at least one of the houses of Congress in the US midterm elections on Tuesday, setting the stage for a potentially volatile ride in the stock and bond markets with artificial intelligence oversight, defense spending and crypto legislation on the table.
Most Read from Bloomberg
A UBS basket of stocks tied to Republicans has plunged since hitting a peak in August, badly lagging the S&P 500 Index. One major area where this could show up is in the AI trade that has been driving the stock market for the past few years, as Democrats are expected to push for stricter regulation and oversight of the technology. Meanwhile, local governments are under pressure to block data centers from being built in their communities.
If the "big political takeaway" from the election is that "data centers are bad, that would be impactful for growth," said Robert Waldner, chief investment officer at Invesco Advisers Inc.
At the same time, other industries could be in the crosshairs. If the Democrats push to rein in defense spending, military contractors would likely feel the pinch. Big banks that have been raking in profits on a flood of deals could face scrutiny. And firms tied to cryptocurrencies are likely to catch some Congressional heat simply based on the industry's close ties to the Trump family.
All of which has some Wall Street pros positioning for selling pressure in stocks and demand for safer government bonds. In addition, many traders appear to be so locked into their positions and their expectations for a closely divided Congress that they're vulnerable to volatile swings.
"Investors are heading into the election long the dollar and short duration, with little protection against volatility – particularly in equity markets," Corpay strategist Karl Schamotta said. "The consensus expects a narrow Democratic victory to produce gridlock in Congress, leaving the president to pursue his objectives through executive action, but there are significant tail risks."
Here are the markets and equity sectors worth watching with just days to go before the vote.
Treasuries
History suggests Congressional gridlock is good for bonds by preventing ambitious policies that increase deficits and raise yields on longer-dated Treasuries. This time, however, bond watchers say any fiscal relief will be limited and unlikely to generate a sustained rally because the deficit, at roughly 6% of the economy, has rarely been this large outside of a recession.
"We have way too much debt that will be reckoned with at some point," said Oliver Chambers, head of fixed income SMA at Clark Capital Management. "But if for the next two years, gridlock means we don't add to it at the same rate we've been adding to it, I think that's a good thing."
A particularly strong showing by Democrats could lead to lower Treasury yields if investors see it as a sign of Americans' appetite for AI regulation, which would pressure tech stocks and dent expectations for economic growth.
The Dollar
Like Treasuries, the dollar could get a boost from a Democratic victory based on the same anticipated stabilizing effect of a split Congress.
Some investors believe a divided government could lead President Donald Trump to lean on policies he can implement unilaterally through executive power. Any escalation with Iran, which Trump has suggested may come after the election, is expected to continue supporting the dollar by driving up energy prices and pushing the Federal Reserve to raise interest rates. New tariffs could also support the US currency by stoking inflation — unless they spark a global "sell America" trade like the one that became popular last year.

item.title: Amazon's AI build-out just pushed its cash burn to a record: Chart of the Day
item.author: Jared Blikre
item.description:
Amazon's AI build-out just pushed its cash burn to a record: Chart of the Day
2026-10-31
Por Jared Blikre
https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/article/amazons-ai-build-out-just-pushed-its-cash-burn-to-a-record-chart-of-the-day-100000920.html
Wall Street spent the week punishing Big Tech's biggest AI spenders. Amazon (AMZN) just posted the deepest cash burn in its history.
Amazon's free cash flow — the cash left after paying for data centers, warehouses, and equipment — was an outflow of more than $42 billion over the 12 months through September, according to its third quarter results released Thursday. That's nearly double the previous record of about $23 billion, set in 2022 after Amazon overbuilt its warehouse network. Three months earlier, the outflow was less than $8 billion.
One quarter did most of the damage. Amazon spent about $77 billion on property and equipment from July through September, more than double the $35 billion it spent a year earlier. Its operations brought in about $42 billion, leaving a gap of roughly $33 billion over three months, according to Yahoo Finance calculations.
So far, the spending is working.
Amazon Web Services (AWS) grew 39% to about $46 billion, its fastest pace in nearly five years, and Amazon's operating margin of nearly 14% was its highest ever. CEO Andy Jassy said in the release that he projects AWS growth of more than 40% in both 2027 and 2028. Anthropic's (ANTH.PVT) computing commitments alone amount to about a fifth of AWS's backlog as of June, according to Yahoo Finance calculations based on the AI lab's IPO filing.
Paying for it has meant borrowing. Amazon's long-term debt reached about $173 billion at the end of September, up from about $66 billion at the end of 2025, while its cash fell to about $56 billion from about $87 billion. Meta (META) took a different route this week with a nearly $100 billion stock sale.
Bond traders have noticed. The cost of insuring Amazon's debt against default for five years with credit default swaps has risen about 50% since early August, according to Bloomberg data. That price implies roughly a 7% chance of default over five years, up from about 5%, according to Yahoo Finance calculations.
Amazon stock fell about 4% Thursday to its lowest close since July 30 as Alphabet's record drop weighed on Big Tech. It slid further after-hours as sales, earnings, and its profit outlook for the holiday quarter missed estimates.
Amazon isn't planning to ease off. CEO Andy Jassy said on the company's earnings call Thursday that Amazon still expects to spend about $220 billion this year, mostly on AWS, and to "spend meaningfully more in 2027."
"Would it be more convenient if this type of acceleration and opportunity happened over 25 years and you could spread the CapEx over 25 years? Yeah, it might be more convenient, but that's not the world that we live in," Jassy said. "We can fund this plan. I think it will forever change the size of Amazon."

item.title: The biggest question about Binance bitcoin heist: How much AI was involved?
item.author: Ethan Wolff-Mann
item.description:
The biggest question about Binance bitcoin heist: How much AI was involved?
2026-10-31
Por Ethan Wolff-Mann
https://finance.yahoo.com/technology/article/the-biggest-question-about-binance-bitcoin-heist-how-much-ai-was-involved-100000500.html
We all woke up on Friday to the news of a heist. Cryptocurrency firm Binance got knocked over to the tune of $6.3 billion in an attack linked to North Korea.
As someone steeped in Hollywood heist genre movies, I cleared my schedule. This is the biggest heist in human history as far as we can tell so far, and certainly the biggest crypto heist.
The company says it will cover the losses and is working with law enforcement to get into the details of a very well-coordinated and complex attack. Around $3 billion has been frozen safe, but a solid chunk of Binance's balance sheet may be gone forever.
It's a news story that brings so many hot-button issues into focus: Crypto regulation. General banking regulation and security in the advancing AI era. Are models like Anthropic's Mythos truly too dangerous for eventual public release, if they could enable a hack like this? Is this a prelude to a new series of weekly smash-and-grabs by AI-powered hackers? Will Paramount Skydance buy the rights to Binance's story for a thriller series?
But first, we need answers to the most critical question: What was the role of AI here?
If it played a big role, is the insurance industry that backstops corporate risk about to get smashed and grabbed too? What does this mean for banks? We all want to know.
I thought about this and looked at the adjacent tab in my browser: a column published Thursday from The Globe and Mail entitled, "'The action is the juice': Why we're living in the golden age of Michael Mann's Heat." (It's not just me who loves heist culture.)
The "how did this happen" will be fascinating.
But juxtaposing this crypto bank job with a real bank job is a stark reminder of how dramatically the world is shifting — and how fast. (And potentially how much people miss that era.)
Especially given the other big news of the week: Google Search's influence is on the decline, eaten by its own AI tools.
Add it to the list of changes and goodbyes: manual transmission, steering wheels, typing over 60 wpm, evaluating information sources, reading comprehension, and more.
And now heists are fully online, done from a country far away, and potentially done entirely by a computer, powered by the AI productivity machine. I can't help but think, "We used to have real heists in this country."
You can see why society loves the poetry of an art theft.
I'll cauterize my brief elegy to the past with the simple forward-looking thought: AI-powered or not, this bitcoin heist and Google's AI cannibalization may both turn out to be parts of the same larger transformation, both representative events for a moment of change.
Ethan Wolff-Mann edits Yahoo Finance's Morning Brief newsletter. Sign up here.

2026-10-31
Por Ethan Wolff-Mann
https://finance.yahoo.com/technology/article/the-biggest-question-about-binance-bitcoin-heist-how-much-ai-was-involved-100000500.html
We all woke up on Friday to the news of a heist. Cryptocurrency firm Binance got knocked over to the tune of $6.3 billion in an attack linked to North Korea.
As someone steeped in Hollywood heist genre movies, I cleared my schedule. This is the biggest heist in human history as far as we can tell so far, and certainly the biggest crypto heist.
The company says it will cover the losses and is working with law enforcement to get into the details of a very well-coordinated and complex attack. Around $3 billion has been frozen safe, but a solid chunk of Binance's balance sheet may be gone forever.
It's a news story that brings so many hot-button issues into focus: Crypto regulation. General banking regulation and security in the advancing AI era. Are models like Anthropic's Mythos truly too dangerous for eventual public release, if they could enable a hack like this? Is this a prelude to a new series of weekly smash-and-grabs by AI-powered hackers? Will Paramount Skydance buy the rights to Binance's story for a thriller series?
But first, we need answers to the most critical question: What was the role of AI here?
If it played a big role, is the insurance industry that backstops corporate risk about to get smashed and grabbed too? What does this mean for banks? We all want to know.
I thought about this and looked at the adjacent tab in my browser: a column published Thursday from The Globe and Mail entitled, "'The action is the juice': Why we're living in the golden age of Michael Mann's Heat." (It's not just me who loves heist culture.)
The "how did this happen" will be fascinating.
But juxtaposing this crypto bank job with a real bank job is a stark reminder of how dramatically the world is shifting — and how fast. (And potentially how much people miss that era.)
Especially given the other big news of the week: Google Search's influence is on the decline, eaten by its own AI tools.
Add it to the list of changes and goodbyes: manual transmission, steering wheels, typing over 60 wpm, evaluating information sources, reading comprehension, and more.
And now heists are fully online, done from a country far away, and potentially done entirely by a computer, powered by the AI productivity machine. I can't help but think, "We used to have real heists in this country."
You can see why society loves the poetry of an art theft.
I'll cauterize my brief elegy to the past with the simple forward-looking thought: AI-powered or not, this bitcoin heist and Google's AI cannibalization may both turn out to be parts of the same larger transformation, both representative events for a moment of change.
Ethan Wolff-Mann edits Yahoo Finance's Morning Brief newsletter. Sign up here.

item.title: Reddit (and everyone else) faces a bleak internet without Google traffic
item.author: Hamza Shaban
item.description:
Reddit (and everyone else) faces a bleak internet without Google traffic
2026-10-31
Por Hamza Shaban
https://finance.yahoo.com/technology/article/reddit-and-everyone-else-faces-a-bleak-internet-without-google-traffic-100000669.html
Google zero, eventually, comes for us all.
That's the belief, and fear, that meaningful traffic from Google trends toward zero because of changes to its search engine practices and, more recently, its shift toward AI — answering people's search questions not with links to places like websites, but with AI summaries and chatbot dialogue.
Reddit's (RDDT) latest earnings report was a reckoning of Google's AI-led changes. And it underscored how Silicon Valley's full embrace of AI may come at the cost of huge swaths of the web — and the companies that rely on Google traffic to operate.
"People still want Reddit. It is just Google is not sending them to Reddit the way they used to," Steve Huffman, Reddit's co-founder and CEO, said on an earnings call earlier this week.
The company reported that search referral traffic was down meaningfully in the past quarter. Google's shift to AI mode and AI overviews has halted traffic that once flowed to the social forum.
Reddit stock fell 30% on Friday.
"Google is crawling us as hard as ever, so the demand hasn't changed from their point of view either," Huffman said. "The reality is the AI Mode does not drive traffic. Not for us, and not to anybody as far as I know."
The shift toward a more AI-inflicted internet isn't just hurting Reddit. It's hurting Google too, at least in the short term. Its parent company, Alphabet (GOOG, GOOGL), shed almost $500 billion (or about two Netflixes) in market value after reporting a slowdown in its core search advertising business, in part due to the lower profitability of AI ads.
A critical view of the whole situation is that Google is smothering online publishers and sabotaging its own legacy business in its rush toward AI dominance.
But Reddit took a stance on the call that could be described as corporate Zen: "For AI Overviews and traffic, look, we don't control Google. We only control Reddit."
The company said it's not counting on that once-sweet Google traffic returning and plans to require all users to create Reddit accounts and sign in to access the site.
Other online publishers are looking to subscriptions to create direct relationships with audiences and are partnering with AI companies to ride the next wave of LLM-based media and product distribution.
Google, for its part, continues to argue the case (although not persuasively, given the stock plunge) that its AI efforts will prevail, even if it's still trying to figure out the problem of how to make more money with it.
Google executives no doubt disagree with the market sell-off, which has dragged the company's price-to-earnings (P/E) ratio back to levels not seen since 2012. Management knew this transition was coming. Their contention is that the success of AI tools will generate a new and different business model, and that it will be more profitable than the search-and-click paradigm the rest of the web relied on.
The bull case is that Google has good reasons to choose this bumpy path. But that also happens to be a bear case for almost everyone else.
Follow Hamza Shaban on X @hshaban.

item.title: Starbucks CEO Brian Niccol: 'The turn has occurred' — now it's in growth mode
item.author: Brian Sozzi
item.description:
Starbucks CEO Brian Niccol: 'The turn has occurred' — now it's in growth mode
2026-10-31
Por Brian Sozzi
https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/article/starbucks-ceo-brian-niccol-the-turn-has-occurred--now-its-in-growth-mode-145654793.html
The turnaround at Starbucks (SBUX) has been served up, and now it looks to be a caffeinated period of growth.
"I think we're back to being just a growth company. I think the turn has occurred. And now we have all these growth opportunities in front of us because we've got a strong foundation," Starbucks CEO Brian Niccol said on Sozzi Unleashed.
Starbucks delivered a bottom-line beat in its fiscal fourth quarter results on Thursday evening, posting adjusted earnings of $0.80 per share versus estimates for $0.71.
Three highlights in particular stood out, in addition to the earnings beat.
Global comparable-store sales jumped 7.2%, and US same-store sales accelerated to 7.7%, driven by healthy ticket and transaction expansion. The company reiterated strength in cold beverages and food.
Sales strength led to a 460 basis point expansion in the operating margin to 14%.
Starbucks also offered initial fiscal 2027 adjusted profit guidance of $3.15 to $3.25 per share, ahead of the $3.14 estimate.
Niccol said the company is full speed ahead on revamping its drive-thrus to unleash the power of AI, offering more caffeine-free afternoon beverages (think drinks with collagen) and new portable foods to match.
"After a strong quarter that showcased significant margin improvement and continued momentum on top-line, we believe Starbucks has raised the bar for excellence," Bernstein analyst Danilo Gargiulo said.

item.title: Intel’s drop on Friday shaves the US government’s equity stake by about $10 billion. It’s still up 3x since last August.
item.author: Ben Werschkul
item.description:
Intel’s drop on Friday shaves the US government’s equity stake by about $10 billion. It’s still up 3x since last August.
2026-10-30
Por Ben Werschkul
https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/article/fridays-rout-shaved-over-11-billion-off-the-us-governments-stake-in-intel-203318952.html
The share price of Intel dropped almost 30% on Friday, shaving over $11 billion from the US government's stake in the company, though the transaction remains profitable overall.
Last August, the Trump administration took a 9.9% equity stake in the chipmaker at a price of $20.47 per share, according to a company press release at the time.
That initial stake of 433.3 million primary shares was worth about $8.9 billion. The value shot up dramatically earlier this year, with Intel (INTC) closing on Thursday at $92.07 per share, implying a value to the US government of $39.9 billion.
But the stock took a beating on Friday after the company reported earnings on Thursday night. The stock closed Friday down about 29% at $65.76 per share, suggesting a new paper value for the government's stake of $28.5 billion.
The rapid price change underscores how government investments can take investors on a wild ride and presents a new challenge to a centerpiece of Trump's government portfolio, which now spans 40 companies, according to a CATO Institute tracker.
A nearly $150 billion loss for the company
Investors punished Intel after its Q4 revenue outlook fell short of Wall Street expectations and the company reported a worse-than-anticipated drop in PC revenue.
Intel is projecting fourth quarter revenue of $15 billion to $16 billion, well below the $17 billion analysts expected. The company is projecting earnings per share of $0.25 versus forecasts of $0.43.
That change in outlook led to losses that, at some points on Friday morning, put Intel on pace for its worst losses since 1974, as the company as a whole erased nearly $150 billion in market value.
The government's investment in Intel — which Trump has promised will yield outsized returns for taxpayers — is a running theme from the White House. In September, an image on Truth Social depicted the president as a stock trader in the Oval Office, with Intel's price displayed on a screen at $95 per share.
Trump has previously exaggerated the gains, suggesting at one point, "I've made Hundreds of Billions of Dollars on Stocks, and many other type Holdings, for the U.S.A., not myself."
Even so, the investment in Intel remains very profitable and still ended the day on Friday more than three times what the US paid for it.
This story has been updated.
Ben Werschkul is a Washington correspondent for Yahoo Finance.

item.title: Intel, Amazon lead tech lower, crypto markets rattled amid $6.3 billion Binance hack: AlphaCheck
item.author: Ines Ferré
item.description:
Intel, Amazon lead tech lower, crypto markets rattled amid $6.3 billion Binance hack: AlphaCheck
2026-10-30
Por Ines Ferré
https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/article/intel-amazon-lead-tech-lower-bitcoin-falls-on-suspected-biggest-crypto-hack-in-history-alphacheck-135624242.html
Good morning. Stocks declined on Friday as shares of chipmaker Intel (INTC) and Amazon (AMZN) led Technology (XLK) and Consumer Discretionary (XLY) stocks lower following their quarterly results.
The declines came after Alphabet (GOOG, GOOGL) stock plunged 12% in the prior session.
Here's a check of the markets in the first few minutes of trading, based on a heat map powered by Yahoo Finance AlphaSpace data.
Crypto markets were rattled on Friday after Binance reported a $6.3 billion breach in what is likely the largest heist in history.
Bitcoin (BTC-USD) prices tumbled to around $77,000. Ether (ETH-USD) also dropped 4% to around $2,200. Crypto-related stocks also opened lower. Shares of Circle (CRCL) and trading platforms Coinbase (COIN) and Robinhood (HOOD) all tumbled. Digital-asset Treasury giant Strategy (MSTR) stock also sank. (Disclosure: Yahoo Finance has a partnership with Coinbase.)
Brent crude oil futures (BZ=F) jumped 2% to hover near $113 per barrel, while WTI (CL=F) also rose to $103.
Here are some other notable stocks that Yahoo Finance readers are viewing this morning: Sandisk (SNDK), Reddit (RDDT), and ExxonMobil (XOM).
Follow Ines Ferré on X at @ines_ferre.

item.title: Alphabet’s October wipeout hits $758 billion, its worst month ever
item.author: Jared Blikre
item.description:
Alphabet’s October wipeout hits $758 billion, its worst month ever
2026-10-30
Por Jared Blikre
https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/article/alphabets-october-wipeout-hits-758-billion-its-worst-month-ever-211521791.html
Big Tech's brutal week had one clear epicenter. Alphabet (GOOGL) lost $468 billion in market value this week, more than SpaceX, Intel and Nvidia combined.
That was the Google parent's worst week ever and the second-biggest weekly wipeout for any US-listed stock, by Yahoo Finance calculations. Only Nvidia (NVDA) has lost more, about $552 billion in the week of Jan. 27, 2025, when China's DeepSeek rattled AI investors. Alphabet's previous worst was about $386 billion in the week ended June 26.
Most of the damage came Thursday, when Alphabet lost $475 billion in a single session after its third quarter results. Friday's slide wiped out the gains the stock had made earlier in the week.
October was even worse. Alphabet shed about $758 billion in market value this month, the second-biggest monthly loss ever for a US-listed company. item.title: The 'Magnificent 7' stocks are seeing stunning declines
item.author: Brian Sozzi
item.description:
The 'Magnificent 7' stocks are seeing stunning declines
2026-10-30
Por Brian Sozzi
https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/article/the-magnificent-7-stocks-are-seeing-stunning-declines-092719792.html
Call it the Unflattering Seven.
Long known as the "Magnificent Seven" stocks, Apple (AAPL), Microsoft (MSFT), Nvidia (NVDA), Amazon (AMZN), Tesla (TSLA), Meta (META), and Google (GOOG, GOOGL) shares are acting anything but, especially compared to their 52-week highs.
Meta and Alphabet are effectively in bear markets, down more than 20% from their 52-week highs, as the Yahoo Finance AlphaSpace graphic below shows. Tesla is off by 19.2%, Amazon by 15.1%, and AI chip darling Nvidia by 12.2%.
Meta, Alphabet, Amazon, and Tesla have been crushed following earnings reports that showed pressured free cash flow amid aggressive AI spending. Nvidia is down due to fears that all these hyperscalers are overspending and will be forced to pull back in 2027.
Apple and Microsoft are the only Magnificent Seven names hanging tough, for company-specific reasons.
Microsoft managed to show positive free cash flow this week alongside strong Azure sales growth. Apple isn't being viewed as an AI play, but more as a cash-rich play rolling out new hardware in the iPhone and Mac realms.
"There is too much weakness in tech for the market to ignore," BTIG strategist Jonathan Krinsky said.
Too much weakness in seven of the world's most important stocks for the market to ignore is more like it.

item.title: Amazon, Alphabet, SpaceX, and Meta are all to blame for the new tech stock rout
item.author: Brian Sozzi
item.description:
Amazon, Alphabet, SpaceX, and Meta are all to blame for the new tech stock rout
2026-10-30
Por Brian Sozzi
https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/article/amazon-alphabet-spacex-and-meta-are-all-to-blame-for-the-new-tech-stock-rout-090324190.html
Don't blame Intel's (INTC) weak guidance, tied to a prolonged memory chip supply shortage, for the fresh rout on tech stocks.
Blame the hyperscalers like Amazon (AMZN), Alphabet (GOOG, GOOGL), and Meta (META) for not properly guiding Wall Street on how much they intend to spend this year and next on AI infrastructure. The bills are coming in much larger than expected, and Wall Street can't stomach it.
That's why you aren't seeing many heroes out there saying buy the dip right now. That's why Friday is shaping up to be another bloodbath for tech stocks.
Remember, it's cash flow that will be used to repay all the debt hyperscalers are poised to incur to support their robust AI infrastructure build-outs. The fact that cash flow is drying up due to a protracted period of spending is the bug that's causing the debt and stock markets to catch a cold.
Kudos to Amazon for at least not burying its free cash flow metric — the most important metric for tech at the moment — at the bottom of its earnings release. It made it no less tough to stomach, but at least it was easy to find quickly.
Amazon's free cash flow decreased to an outflow of $42.4 billion for the trailing 12 months, driven primarily by a year-over-year increase of $94.8 billion in purchases of property and equipment. This increase primarily reflects investments in artificial intelligence, Amazon said.
This compares to a free cash flow inflow of $14.8 billion for the trailing 12 months ended Sept. 30 of last year.
"We still expect 2026 cash capex of approximately $220 billion, the majority for AWS, and expect to spend meaningfully more in 2027," Amazon CEO Andy Jassy said on his earnings call.
Amazon stock is down 7% in premarket trading today.
On Wednesday evening, Google posted negative free cash flow of $9.1 billion in the quarter versus Wall Street's estimate for negative $3.5 billion.
Thursday saw more than $500 billion in market value wiped off Google.
Meta dropped a bombshell in its third quarter results last week, posting negative free cash flow for the first time since 2012. SpaceX (SPCX) burned about $9.9 billion in free cash flow in the quarter.
Both stocks have continued to sell off post-earnings.
Hyperscaler free cash flow is likely to stay negative, Evercore ISI strategist Julian Emanuel pointed out. The hyperscaler cohort of Meta, Amazon, Google, Microsoft, Oracle (ORCL), and SpaceX (SPCX) is now expected to be near $200 billion in losses over the next year, Emanuel's research shows.
This is what the market is pricing in today. Painful, yes.
item.content:encoded:
Amazon, Alphabet, SpaceX, and Meta are all to blame for the new tech stock rout

2026-10-30

Por Brian Sozzi

https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/article/amazon-alphabet-spacex-and-meta-are-all-to-blame-for-the-new-tech-stock-rout-090324190.html

Don't blame Intel's (INTC) weak guidance, tied to a prolonged memory chip supply shortage, for the fresh rout on tech stocks.

Blame the hyperscalers like Amazon (AMZN), Alphabet (GOOG, GOOGL), and Meta (META) for not properly guiding Wall Street on how much they intend to spend this year and next on AI infrastructure. The bills are coming in much larger than expected, and Wall Street can't stomach it.

That's why you aren't seeing many heroes out there saying buy the dip right now. That's why Friday is shaping up to be another bloodbath for tech stocks.

Remember, it's cash flow that will be used to repay all the debt hyperscalers are poised to incur to support their robust AI infrastructure build-outs. The fact that cash flow is drying up due to a protracted period of spending is the bug that's causing the debt and stock markets to catch a cold.

Kudos to Amazon for at least not burying its free cash flow metric — the most important metric for tech at the moment — at the bottom of its earnings release. It made it no less tough to stomach, but at least it was easy to find quickly.

Amazon's free cash flow decreased to an outflow of $42.4 billion for the trailing 12 months, driven primarily by a year-over-year increase of $94.8 billion in purchases of property and equipment. This increase primarily reflects investments in artificial intelligence, Amazon said.

This compares to a free cash flow inflow of $14.8 billion for the trailing 12 months ended Sept. 30 of last year.

"We still expect 2026 cash capex of approximately $220 billion, the majority for AWS, and expect to spend meaningfully more in 2027," Amazon CEO Andy Jassy said on his earnings call.

Amazon stock is down 7% in premarket trading today.

On Wednesday evening, Google posted negative free cash flow of $9.1 billion in the quarter versus Wall Street's estimate for negative $3.5 billion.

Thursday saw more than $500 billion in market value wiped off Google.

Meta dropped a bombshell in its third quarter results last week, posting negative free cash flow for the first time since 2012. SpaceX (SPCX) burned about $9.9 billion in free cash flow in the quarter.

Both stocks have continued to sell off post-earnings.

Hyperscaler free cash flow is likely to stay negative, Evercore ISI strategist Julian Emanuel pointed out. The hyperscaler cohort of Meta, Amazon, Google, Microsoft, Oracle (ORCL), and SpaceX (SPCX) is now expected to be near $200 billion in losses over the next year, Emanuel's research shows.

This is what the market is pricing in today. Painful, yes.

item.description:
Nuestros próximos pasos — y un año gratis para los suscriptores de pago
2026-10-30
Por Newsletter
¡Hola, familia!
Una actualización rápida sobre dónde estamos — y hacia dónde vamos.
La verdad es que ha sido un año muy difícil.
Por un lado, ha sido realmente bueno para Fidelius. Más familias. Más proyectos. Más trabajo. Estamos agradecidos por todo, y es un recordatorio diario de por qué escribimos: las ideas de
Las Empresas Familiares Son Mejores
de verdad FUNCIONAN para las familias empresarias.
Y firmamos un contrato con la editorial perfecta para publicar mi primer libro. Es otra de las cosas que nos mantuvo ocupados y nos sumó trabajo — del mejor tipo. Más noticias del libro más adelante.
Por otro lado, ha sido muy duro para nosotros como familia. Lamentablemente, tuvimos una muerte en la familia, nos mudamos a una casa nueva, y hemos enfrentado varios retos más que, naturalmente, nos exigieron mucho tiempo y atención.
Hemos estado tan sobrecargados que llevo casi tres meses sin publicar contenido nuevo, aunque nuestra meta era publicar “al menos una vez por semana”. Ha sido frustrante no poder escribirte. Pero nuestro compromiso con este trabajo, y CONTIGO, es mayor que nunca. Tuvimos una época difícil, pero ya está terminando y estamos volviendo al trabajo.
Hacia dónde vamos
Estamos orgullosos de lo que hemos construido hasta ahora. Y queremos hacer MUCHO más. Esto es lo que significa:
Nuevos tipos de contenido, porque todos aprendemos mejor con variedad.
Más video. Hay cosas que simplemente se dicen mejor en voz alta.
Contenido más frecuente: un ritmo con el que puedes contar.
Más valor para lectores gratuitos Y de pago.
Más fácil de leer, más fácil de poner en práctica.
Porque la meta no es que leas sobre empresas familiares. Es ayudarte a mejorar TU PROPIA familia y empresas.
Vamos a experimentar. Algunas cosas funcionarán, y otras no. Seguiremos aprendiendo, y seguiremos mejorando.
Quiénes hacen esto posible
Podríamos publicar este boletín de Substack gratis. Tenemos los recursos para hacerlo fácilmente.
Lo que NO tenemos son los recursos para construir nuestra verdadera visión: enseñarles a millones de personas cómo mejorar sus empresas familiares, con una serie completa de cursos y material educativo. Como dice el dicho, se necesita una tribu. Y parte importante de esa tribu eres TÚ, con tu apoyo.
Nuestros suscriptores de pago son más que suscriptores. Son los Pioneros: los primeros en sumarse, los innovadores, quienes están poniendo la primera piedra y los cimientos de todo lo que vamos a construir. Son parte de algo MAYOR. Son líderes.
Estamos muy, muy agradecidos. Juntos, vamos a lograr cosas increíbles.
Y te lo prometemos: cada dólar de los ingresos por suscripciones que llega a nuestras manos se reinvierte en crear más y mejor contenido.
Nos enfocamos en el impacto, no en las ganancias.
Nuestro agradecimiento para los suscriptores de pago
SIEMPRE nos aseguraremos de que nuestros suscriptores reciban más de lo que pagan. Así que si hoy eres suscriptor de pago, te daremos las gracias de una de dos maneras (a tu elección):
Un AÑO completo agregado a tu suscripción, sin costo. Es automático — no tienes que hacer nada.
O un reembolso completo de tu último pago, si lo prefieres. Solo responde a este correo y avísame.
Conviértete en Pionero
Nuestros primeros 1,000 suscriptores de pago son nuestros Pioneros — el primer 0.1% del millón de personas a las que queremos llegar.
Cómo te reconocemos depende de cuándo te unas:
Fundadores — los primeros 100. Quedan 73 lugares.
Pilares — los siguientes 150.
Constructores — los siguientes 750.
¿Ya eres suscriptor de pago? Entonces eres Fundador, y ese título es tuyo para siempre. Una vez Pionero, siempre Pionero. Y todos los Pioneros reciben:
Reconocimiento.
Tu nombre, escrito como TÚ elijas, en la página Nuestra Visión y en mi primer libro — si así lo decides (tu privacidad siempre se respeta). Además, un número de Pionero permanente.
Un

La verdad es que ha sido un año muy difícil.
Por un lado, ha sido realmente bueno para Fidelius. Más familias. Más proyectos. Más trabajo. Estamos agradecidos por todo, y es un recordatorio diario de por qué escribimos: las ideas de
Las Empresas Familiares Son Mejores
de verdad FUNCIONAN para las familias empresarias.
Y firmamos un contrato con la editorial perfecta para publicar mi primer libro. Es otra de las cosas que nos mantuvo ocupados y nos sumó trabajo — del mejor tipo. Más noticias del libro más adelante.
Por otro lado, ha sido muy duro para nosotros como familia. Lamentablemente, tuvimos una muerte en la familia, nos mudamos a una casa nueva, y hemos enfrentado varios retos más que, naturalmente, nos exigieron mucho tiempo y atención.
Hemos estado tan sobrecargados que llevo casi tres meses sin publicar contenido nuevo, aunque nuestra meta era publicar “al menos una vez por semana”. Ha sido frustrante no poder escribirte. Pero nuestro compromiso con este trabajo, y CONTIGO, es mayor que nunca. Tuvimos una época difícil, pero ya está terminando y estamos volviendo al trabajo.
Hacia dónde vamos
Estamos orgullosos de lo que hemos construido hasta ahora. Y queremos hacer MUCHO más. Esto es lo que significa:
Nuevos tipos de contenido, porque todos aprendemos mejor con variedad.
Más video. Hay cosas que simplemente se dicen mejor en voz alta.
Contenido más frecuente: un ritmo con el que puedes contar.
Más valor para lectores gratuitos Y de pago.
Más fácil de leer, más fácil de poner en práctica.
Porque la meta no es que leas sobre empresas familiares. Es ayudarte a mejorar TU PROPIA familia y empresas.
Vamos a experimentar. Algunas cosas funcionarán, y otras no. Seguiremos aprendiendo, y seguiremos mejorando.
Quiénes hacen esto posible
Podríamos publicar este boletín de Substack gratis. Tenemos los recursos para hacerlo fácilmente.
Lo que NO tenemos son los recursos para construir nuestra verdadera visión: enseñarles a millones de personas cómo mejorar sus empresas familiares, con una serie completa de cursos y material educativo. Como dice el dicho, se necesita una tribu. Y parte importante de esa tribu eres TÚ, con tu apoyo.
Nuestros suscriptores de pago son más que suscriptores. Son los Pioneros: los primeros en sumarse, los innovadores, quienes están poniendo la primera piedra y los cimientos de todo lo que vamos a construir. Son parte de algo MAYOR. Son líderes.
Estamos muy, muy agradecidos. Juntos, vamos a lograr cosas increíbles.
Y te lo prometemos: cada dólar de los ingresos por suscripciones que llega a nuestras manos se reinvierte en crear más y mejor contenido.
Nos enfocamos en el impacto, no en las ganancias.

item.title: North Korean hackers likelinked to record-breaking $6.3 billion Binance crypto heist
item.author: Ines Ferré
item.description:
North Korean hackers likelinked to record-breaking $6.3 billion Binance crypto heist
2026-10-30
Por Ines Ferré
https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/article/bitcoin-drops-to-76000-as-binance-hack-spooks-investors-tether-circle-freeze-assets-083406383.html
Binance, the world's largest cryptocurrency exchange, was hit late Thursday by what investigators say is the biggest crypto hack in history, with $6.3 billion in funds impacted and roughly half of those assets frozen.
Customer withdrawals have been temporarily suspended, and co-CEO Richard Teng promised the exchange will cover all losses.
"We are committed to covering all hacked losses through our company funds. Your assets are safe," Teng said on social media.
Binance said it has money set aside in a Secure Asset Fund for Users to handle extreme cases, such as security breaches.
$6.3 billion Binance hack shakes crypto industry
Here's what you need to know:
Binance co-CEO Yi He said in a separate social media post Friday morning that customer withdrawals should resume within 48 hours.
"We are rebuilding the withdrawal service, and we are not switching it back until it passes rigorous testing," noted Teng on Friday. "We are very hopeful that users will be able to withdraw prior to the Sunday deadline."
Teng said the hack was not carried out by one person. Initial findings pointed to a compromised laptop, but further review revealed broader security breaches.
"This was a complex attack," Teng said. "The attacker also used a self-destruct mechanism that destroyed tooling and tracers."
The attack has rattled crypto markets and related stocks. Bitcoin (BTC-USD) tumbled 5% to hover below $77,000 on Friday.
Other major crypto assets also tumbled after the hack, with ether (ETH-USD) dropping 4% to around $2,200. Binance's native token, BNB (BND-USD), also plunged by more than 6%.
Crypto-related stocks traded lower, led by shares of Circle, trading platforms Coinbase (COIN) and Robinhood (HOOD), and digital-asset Treasury giant Strategy (MSTR).
Binance said that about $3 billion in assets have been "frozen on-chain so far."
The frozen assets include over $2 billion in stablecoins. Tether, the world's largest stablecoin issuer, "froze more than 1.567B" of its USDT stablecoin in relation to the hack," CEO Paolo Ardoino said on X. The second-largest issuer, Circle (CRCL), froze another $800 million "in coordination with law enforcement," CEO Jeremy Allaire said. World Liberty Financial, a cryptocurrency venture co-founded by President Trump and his sons, said it froze $27 million of its stablecoin, USD1, associated with the hack, according to CEO Zack Witkoff.
Although details are still emerging, the hack is shaping up to be the largest crypto theft in history, far exceeding the previous record set in February 2025, when attackers stole $1.5 billion from the crypto derivatives exchange ByBit.
